| `input_dir` | path | Flat directory of bronze `.h5ad` files to process |
| `output_base_dir` | path | Silver-tier root; one subdirectory is created per dataset |
| `dev_stage_map` / `tissue_map` / `disease_map` | pickle paths | Obs-column vocabulary maps applied via `Series.map` |
| `excluded_file` + `do_exclude_file` | str + bool | Opt-in skip of a single named file |
| `gene_filtering.remove_ensembl_txt` | CSV path | Ensembl IDs to unconditionally drop (e.g., non-coding) |
| `gene_filtering.ensembl_mapping_dict` | pickle path | Gene-name dictionary; LINC/MIR entries pruned, remainder kept |

All paths in the shipped config are absolute NFS paths (`/nfs/team361/...`), which reflects that this stage runs on the lab's cluster storage rather than against repo-relative paths.

Sources: [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L13-L15), [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L206-L212), [config_am74.yaml](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/config_am74.yaml#L1-L11)

### Metadata Vocabulary Harmonization

The core harmonization problem at cohort scale is vocabulary drift: each source study annotates `development_stage`, `tissue`, and `disease` with its own ontology terms. The pipeline resolves this by dictionary remapping rather than hard-coded rules — the three pickles loaded in `harmonize_dataset` are lookup tables from raw terms to canonical ones. The remapping semantics are **map-then-fillna**: unmatched values fall through to their original strings rather than being dropped, so no cell is lost to a stale dictionary, and provenance is preserved by writing canonical values into `trace_*` columns while `tissue` is overwritten in place.

| `obs` column | Origin | Transformation | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trace_dev_stage` | `development_stage` | `map(dev_stage_map)` | Original value via `fillna` |
| `tissue` | `tissue` | `map(tissue_map)`, in place | Original value via `fillna` |
| `trace_disease` | `disease` | `map(disease_map)` | `"unknown"` if the column is absent entirely |
| `study` | Filename stem | Literal string assignment | — |

The `study` column derived from the filename is what makes the silver tier self-documenting at the cell level: every downstream analysis can attribute a cell to its source dataset without external manifests. Note that if a dataset lacks a `disease` column the script logs a warning and stamps `trace_disease="unknown"` — the harmonized schema is total, not optional.

Sources: [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L147-L165), [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L171-L192), [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L194-L198)

### Gene Filtering Strategy

Gene-space unification uses two independent masks applied sequentially inside `perform_qc` when the `gene_filtering` config block is present. The first mask is a **blocklist**: a CSV of Ensembl "Gene stable ID" values (non-coding and low-quality loci) is loaded into a set and subtracted from `var['ensembl_id']`. The second mask is an **allowlist**: the Ensembl mapping dictionary (the same `ensembl_mapping_dict_gc95M` family shipped in `perturbgen/pp/`) is filtered to drop keys beginning with `LINC` or `MIR`, and only genes whose `feature_name` survives that filter are retained. Only after both masks pass is the gene universe aligned with the token dictionary used in stage 3 — a dataset whose genes are not in this intersection would tokenize with missing tokens.

> [!TIP]
> The two masks are complementary, not redundant: the blocklist removes unwanted Ensembl IDs even when a gene *name* maps, while the allowlist removes genes with no mapping at all. Editing `remove_ensembl_txt` is the supported extension point for cohort-specific exclusions without touching code.

Sources: [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L47-L49), [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L51-L79)

### Raw-Count Provenance and Cell-Level QC

Before QC, the script repairs count provenance with a heuristic: if `adata.X.max() < 50`, the matrix is assumed to be normalized, and the script attempts to restore raw counts first from `adata.raw.X`, then from `adata.layers["counts"]`. QC annotation flags mitochondrial, ribosomal, and hemoglobin genes by `feature_name` prefixes (`MT-`, `RPS`/`RPL`, `^HB[^(P)]`), then `sc.pp.calculate_qc_metrics` computes the per-cell statistics that the outlier gates consume. Outlier detection is **median-absolute-deviation (MAD) based** rather than fixed-threshold based, implemented as a local `is_outlier` closure over `scipy.stats.median_abs_deviation` — this makes the gates adaptive to each dataset's count distribution, which is essential when the cohort mixes 10x, SS2, and other protocols.

| QC gate | Metric(s) | Threshold | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Provenance repair | `X.max()` | `< 50` → restore `raw.X` or `layers["counts"]` | Guarantees raw counts downstream |
| General outlier | `log1p_total_counts`, `log1p_n_genes_by_counts`, `pct_counts_in_top_20_genes` | ±5 MADs (any metric) | Drop cell |
| Mitochondrial outlier | `pct_counts_mt` | ±4 MADs or absolute > 20% | Drop cell |
| Sparse genes | Cells expressing gene | `min_cells=5` | Drop gene |
| Post-QC bookkeeping | Row sums of final `X` | — | Written to `obs['n_counts']` |

Two details matter operationally. First, the mitochondrial gate combines a statistical test with a hard 20% ceiling, so dead cells are removed even in datasets with tight distributions. Second, if a dataset lacks `feature_name`, mt/ribo/hb flags are silently set to `False` and their metrics become uninformative — the warning is printed but processing continues. After filtering, the surviving matrix is written as `{stem}_qc.h5ad` into a per-dataset subdirectory of `output_base_dir`, and `del adata; gc.collect()` bounds peak memory between datasets.

> [!TIP]
> The raw-counts check is silent-degradation tolerant: a bronze file with neither `raw` nor a `counts` layer proceeds with whatever is in `X`, and the only signal is the log line `"No raw or counts layer found"`. When auditing a new cohort, grep the harmonization logs for that string — such files will corrupt the median statistics of stage 2.

Sources: [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L32-L49), [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L81-L103), [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L105-L144), [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L200-L203)

### Launching Harmonization

`launch_harmonize.sh` is the cluster entry point. It takes the config path as its first positional argument, activates the `scanpy` conda environment from the `cellgen` environment-modules system for a hardcoded list of users, then invokes the harmonization script. Because the interpreter path inside the script is an absolute NFS path, running it elsewhere requires editing that line — the script is infrastructure-coupled by design, not portable.

```bash
bash pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/launch_harmonize.sh /path/to/config_am74.yaml
```

Sources: [launch_harmonize.sh](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/launch_harmonize.sh#L1-L16)

## Stage 2: Cohort-Wide Median Statistics via Mergeable TDigests

Stage 2 answers a question stage 3 depends on: *for each gene, what is the median scaled expression across the entire cohort?* Computing this naively would require either holding every dataset's expression matrix in memory or a two-pass sort. The implementation instead uses **t-digests** (`crick.tdigest.TDigest`) — mergeable quantile sketches that approximate arbitrary quantiles (including the median) with bounded memory. This splits stage 2 into an embarrassingly parallel map and a cheap serial reduce, mirroring the map-reduce pattern: `median_calculation_1.py` produces one sketch dictionary per input file, and `aggregate_medians.py` merges all of them.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    F1["Silver file 1"] -->|"CP10K normalize<br/>densify"| K1["TDigest per gene<br/>(nonzero values only)"]
    F2["Silver file 2"] -->|"CP10K normalize<br/>densify"| K2["TDigest per gene"]
    FN["Silver file N"] -->|"CP10K normalize<br/>densify"| KN["TDigest per gene"]
    K1 & K2 & KN --> MG["merge_digest:<br/>TDigest.merge (order-independent)"]
    MG --> Q["quantile(0.5) per gene"]
    Q --> A1["total_gene_tdigest_dict.pickle"]
    Q --> A2["total_gene_median_dict.pickle"]
    Q --> A3["detected_gene_median_dict.pickle<br/>(NaN medians dropped)"]
```

Sources: [median_calculation_1.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/median_calculation_1.py#L1-L14), [aggregate_medians.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/aggregate_medians.py#L5-L37)

### Map Step: Per-File Sketch Construction

`median_calculation_1.py` walks the silver-tier tree recursively, and for each `.h5ad`: reads the gene identifiers from `var['ensembl_id']`, densifies the (possibly sparse) expression matrix, and normalizes per cell to counts-per-10k using the `n_counts` column that stage 1 wrote to `obs` — this is why stage 1's bookkeeping column is a hard dependency of stage 2. For each gene column it extracts the non-zero values as `float32` and updates a dedicated TDigest; zero-valued entries are excluded so that the median reflects the expression distribution of *detected* cells, not the sparsity pattern. Each file yields `{stem}.gene_median_digest_dict.pickle` mapping Ensembl ID → sketch. Every file is wrapped in try/except/finally with `gc.collect()`, so one corrupt file cannot abort the cohort scan.

Sources: [median_calculation_1.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/median_calculation_1.py#L16-L33), [median_calculation_1.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/median_calculation_1.py#L35-L47), [median_calculation_1.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/median_calculation_1.py#L48-L63)

### Reduce Step: Aggregation and Median Extraction

`aggregate_medians.py` walks the sketch output directory, merges every per-gene sketch into a running total (sketches are order-independent, so traversal order does not affect results), and emits three pickles in a single pass: the merged sketch dictionary itself, the extracted medians via `quantile(0.5)`, and a *detected-genes* dictionary that filters out `NaN` medians — a gene whose median is `NaN` was never observed with a non-zero value anywhere in the cohort and is therefore not detectable. Unlike stage 1, both scripts of stage 2 are constants-driven: input and output directories are hardcoded at module level and are edited per cohort rather than passed on the command line.

| Artifact | Producer | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `{stem}.gene_median_digest_dict.pickle` | `median_calculation_1.py` | Per-gene TDigest (CP10K, non-zero values) |
| `total_gene_tdigest_dict.pickle` | `aggregate_medians.py` | Cohort-merged sketches (reusable for other quantiles) |
| `total_gene_median_dict.pickle` | `aggregate_medians.py` | `quantile(0.5)` per gene — the normalization vocabulary |
| `detected_gene_median_dict.pickle` | `aggregate_medians.py` | Median dict with `NaN` entries removed |

> [!TIP]
> Because the reduce step is a pure merge of persisted sketches, the map step can be distributed across any number of workers or rerun incrementally as new studies arrive — just point `merge_all_tdigests` at a directory containing all sketch pickles. There is no global pass over the cohort; adding a dataset never invalidates previously computed sketches.

Sources: [aggregate_medians.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/aggregate_medians.py#L18-L37), [aggregate_medians.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/aggregate_medians.py#L39-L50), [aggregate_medians.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/aggregate_medians.py#L53-L61)

## Stage 3: Geneformer Tokenization of the Silver Cohort

Stage 3 delegates to Geneformer's `TranscriptomeTokenizer` rather than reimplementing rank-value encoding — the pipeline's job here is wiring: supplying the cohort-specific median dictionary from stage 2, the token dictionary, and the Ensembl mapping file, and carrying the harmonized metadata through. The tokenizer is constructed with custom attributes `{"tissue": "tissue", "disease": "disease"}` — exactly the `obs` columns stage 1 harmonized — so the silver-tier annotations propagate into the tokenized dataset records. The context size is set to `model_input_size=4096` with 32 worker processes, and HF `datasets` caching is disabled globally and the cache directory is force-removed after every file to prevent cache growth while iterating a large cohort.

| Parameter | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Custom attributes | `tissue`, `disease` | Harmonized `obs` columns carried into tokenized records |
| `model_input_size` | `4096` | Maximum genes per rank-encoded cell transcript |
| `gene_median_file` | Stage-2 median pickle | Per-gene normalization references |
| `token_dictionary_file` | Cohort token dict | Gene → token-ID vocabulary |
| `gene_mapping_file` | Ensembl mapping dict | Gene-name/ID alignment |
| `nproc` | `32` | Parallel tokenization workers |
| `use_generator` | `True` | Streaming write, no full in-memory dataset |

The mechanics of what the tokenizer does with these inputs — rank-value encoding, median scaling, attribute embedding — belong to the tokenization design itself; see [Geneformer-Style Gene Tokenization](9-geneformer-style-gene-tokenization) for that treatment, and [Tokenized Dataset Layout](16-tokenized-dataset-layout) for the on-disk format these shards take. Each file is tokenized in its own try/except so a failure is logged and skipped rather than aborting the cohort.

Sources: [tokenization.py](pretraining_cohort/tokenization/tokenization.py#L4-L11), [tokenization.py](pretraining_cohort/tokenization/tokenization.py#L13-L21), [tokenization.py](pretraining_cohort/tokenization/tokenization.py#L27-L42)

## End-to-End Execution Walkthrough

A full cohort pass runs the three stages in strict order — stage 2's medians must exist before stage 3 constructs its tokenizer, and stage 3 reads the silver files stage 1 wrote. The following flowchart is the operational checklist; each numbered node is one command or one edited-constants deployment.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["1 · Author cohort YAML<br/>(input/output roots, vocab pickles,<br/>gene_filtering assets)"] --> B["2 · bash launch_harmonize.sh config.yaml"]
    B --> C{"For each .h5ad<br/>in input_dir"}
    C --> D["Map obs vocab<br/>(map + fillna semantics)"]
    D --> E["Gene filtering:<br/>blocklist − non-coding,<br/>allowlist − LINC/MIR"]
    E --> F["MAD cell QC,<br/>min_cells=5 gene filter,<br/>write n_counts"]
    F --> G["Write {stem}_qc.h5ad<br/>to per-dataset subdir"]
    G --> H["3 · median_calculation_1.py<br/>(per-file TDigest map)"]
    H --> I["4 · aggregate_medians.py<br/>(merge reduce → median dicts)"]
    I --> J["5 · tokenization.py<br/>(TranscriptomeTokenizer over silver tree)"]
    J --> K["Tokenized shards →<br/>pretraining input"]
```

Operationally, the stages differ in how they are parameterized, and this asymmetry is intentional: stage 1 is fully config-driven for cohort portability, while stages 2 and 3 pin their artifact paths at the top of each script — you edit constants once per cohort deployment.

| Aspect | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Stage 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parameterization | YAML config file | Hardcoded module constants | Hardcoded module constants |
| Traversal | `os.listdir` (flat bronze dir) | `os.walk` (recursive silver tree) | `os.walk` (recursive silver tree) |
| Failure policy | Per-file `try/except` + `gc` | Per-file `try/except` + `gc` | Per-file `try/except` + cache wipe |
| Primary output | `{stem}_qc.h5ad` per dataset | Sketch and median pickles | Tokenized dataset shards |
| Execution entry | `launch_harmonize.sh` | `python median_calculation_1.py` then `aggregate_medians.py` | `python tokenization.py` |

Sources: [config_am74.yaml](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/config_am74.yaml#L1-L11), [launch_harmonize.sh](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/launch_harmonize.sh#L1-L16), [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L158-L165), [median_calculation_1.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/median_calculation_1.py#L17-L19), [tokenization.py](pretraining_cohort/tokenization/tokenization.py#L27-L42)

## Design Rationale: Why Map-Reduce and Dictionary Remapping

Two architectural choices dominate this pipeline, and both are consequences of cohort scale. First, **vocabulary unification is data, not code**: dev-stage, tissue, and disease harmonization are pickle lookup tables rather than if/else chains, so adapting the pipeline to a new cohort means shipping new pickles — the code path never changes. The `fillna`-preserving semantics mean dictionaries can be incomplete without cell loss. Second, **all cohort-wide statistics flow through mergeable sketches**: the median — a global statistic — is computed as a merge of per-file sketches, giving stage 2 the same resumability and incremental-growth properties as the rest of the pipeline.

| Concern | Naive approach | This pipeline's approach |
|---|---|---|
| Ontology drift across studies | Per-study normalization code | Pickle vocab maps + `trace_*` provenance columns |
| Cohort-wide median | Global sort or two passes over all matrices | Mergeable TDigests: parallel map, O(1)-memory-per-gene reduce |
| Undetected genes | Median = 0 or error | `NaN` filter → `detected_gene_median_dict` |
| One bad input file | Pipeline abort | Per-file `try/except` isolation, cohort continues |
| Memory pressure | Load whole cohort | Per-dataset lifecycle with `del` + `gc.collect()` |
| Count provenance | Trust `X` | `X.max() < 50` heuristic with `raw.X` / `counts` layer fallback |

Sources: [harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py#L171-L192), [median_calculation_1.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/median_calculation_1.py#L35-L47), [aggregate_medians.py](pretraining_cohort/median_calculation/aggregate_medians.py#L39-L50)

## Pipeline Outputs and Downstream Assets

Stage 2's artifact triple — a median dictionary, a token dictionary, and an Ensembl mapping dictionary — is exactly the class of assets the package itself ships for inference and training in `perturbgen/pp/` (`gene_median_dict_gftokens_gc95M.pkl`, `token_dict_gftokens_gc95M.pkl`, `ensembl_mapping_dict_gc95M.pkl`). In other words, this pipeline is the upstream factory for the normalization vocabulary the model consumes; running it against a new cohort yields a new vocabulary without changing any model code. The tokenized cohort produced by stage 3 is the pretraining input — the training checkpoint stored at the root of `pretraining_cohort/` (a masked-generative pretraining run on the `cellgen` cohort) is the downstream consumer this pipeline was built to feed. For how these assets are consumed at training time, continue to [Tokenized Dataset Layout](16-tokenized-dataset-layout) and [Pretrained Checkpoints and Hugging Face Assets](23-pretrained-checkpoints-and-hugging-face-assets); for the upstream curation that decides *which* studies enter the bronze tier, see [Cell Pairing and Data Curation](14-cell-pairing-and-data-curation).


# Tokenized Dataset Layout



This page documents the **on-disk contract** between PerturbGen's tokenization pipelines and its training stack: the storage format of tokenized corpora, the schema of an individual tokenized cell, the pickle artifact registry shipped with the package, the directory naming conventions produced by `GF_tokenisation.py`, and the loading contracts that `train.py` and `PerturbGenDataModule` depend on. This is a layout-focused deep dive: the tokenization algorithm itself is covered in [Geneformer-Style Gene Tokenization](9-geneformer-style-gene-tokenization), cell pairing logic in [Cell Pairing and Data Curation](14-cell-pairing-and-data-curation), upstream cohort preparation in [Pretraining Cohort Harmonization Pipeline](15-pretraining-cohort-harmonization-pipeline), and path management internals in [Configuration System and Path Management](17-configuration-system-and-path-management).

Sources: [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L400-L435), [GF_tokenisation.py](perturbgen/pp/GF_tokenisation.py#L213-L528), [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L331-L399)

## Storage Format: Hugging Face `datasets` Directories

Every tokenized corpus in PerturbGen persists as a **`.dataset` directory** in Hugging Face `datasets` (Arrow) format, written by `Dataset.save_to_disk`. The `TranscriptomeTokenizer.tokenize_data` method terminates by resolving `(output_directory / output_prefix).with_suffix(".dataset")` and calling `save_to_disk` on it, so each output is a self-contained, memory-mappable directory rather than a single file. The pretraining cohort script follows the same convention at scale: it walks every `h5ad` under the harmonized input tree, tokenizes each with `use_generator=True`, and calls `disable_caching()` plus explicit cache cleanup after each file so that no intermediate Arrow cache accumulates on disk.

| Schema column | Type | Presence | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input_ids` | `Sequence(int)` | Always | Rank-coded gene token sequence (see next section) |
| `length` | `int` | Always | Final sequence length after truncation and special-token insertion |
| `input_ids_uncropped` / `length_uncropped` | `Sequence(int)` / `int` | Only if `keep_uncropped_input_ids=True` | Sequence before truncation to `model_input_size` |
| Custom metadata (e.g. `tissue`, `disease`, `Time_point`, `cell_pairing_index`) | Scalar per cell | If `custom_attr_name_dict` supplied | Cell-level attributes carried from `obs` into dataset columns |

Sources: [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L400-L435), [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L632-L685), [tokenization.py](pretraining_cohort/tokenization/tokenization.py#L22-L42)

The schema is constructed in `create_dataset`: a `dict` of `{"input_ids": tokenized_cells}` merged with the metadata columns, converted via `Dataset.from_dict` (or `from_generator` for memory-bounded tokenization), then passed through a `format_cell_features` map that truncates and stamps `length`. Because consumers load these directories with `load_from_disk` and index them per-cell (`dataset[ind]` returning a dict of columns), the Arrow layout gives the datamodule zero-copy random access to individual cells, which is what makes index-based train/val/test splitting cheap.

Sources: [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L632-L685), [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L59-L84)

## Anatomy of a Token Record Sequence

Each `input_ids` entry is a **rank-value encoding**: the cell's raw counts are normalized per-cell to a target sum of 10,000 and divided by per-gene median expression values (`X_view / n_counts * target_sum / norm_factor_vector`), masked to detected genes only, and the surviving gene tokens are sorted **descending by median-scaled expression** via `rank_genes` (`np.argsort(-gene_vector)`). Position in the sequence therefore encodes relative expression magnitude, while the token ID itself encodes gene identity — the two axes the transformer consumes separately.

Sources: [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L526-L532), [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L603-L613)

> [!TIP]
> The sort is the semantic payload: `input_ids[0]` (after the CLS token) is the *most-expressed* gene, not a fixed gene. Any downstream code that assumes positional gene identity (e.g. positional embeddings, per-position decoders) must not treat indices as gene slots — the perturbation decoder instead remaps token IDs to a stable row space via `tokenid_to_rowid` (see below).

For the **95M model series**, the layout includes special tokens: `create_dataset` truncates the ranked sequence to `model_input_size - 2`, then inserts `<cls>` at position 0 and `<eos>` at the end, with `special_token=True` validated against the token dictionary at tokenizer construction. For the **30M series**, no special tokens are added and truncation is to the full `model_input_size`. The datamodule independently re-derives these IDs from the shipped token dictionary (`gene_token_dict.get('<pad>')`, `<cls>`, `<eos>`) so that collation never hardcodes numeric IDs.

| Setting | 95M series | 30M series |
|---|---|---|
| `special_token` | `True` (adds `<cls>` … `<eos>`) | `False` |
| `model_input_size` | 4096 | 2048 |
| Truncation before specials | `input_size - 2` | `input_size` |
| Vocabulary | `token_dict_gftokens_gc95M.pkl` | separate 30M dictionary |

Sources: [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L663-L678), [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L360-L376), [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L319-L324), [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L200-L203)

## Artifact Registry: Pickles Shipped in `perturbgen/pp/`

Three pickle dictionaries are versioned inside the package and serve as the **default vocabulary assets** for both tokenization tracks. `perturbgen/pp/__init__.py` resolves them to absolute paths at import time, and both the tokenizer defaults and `configs/paths.py` point at these constants — meaning the token-ID space of any `.dataset` directory is pinned to the dictionary that produced it.

| File | Key → Value structure | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `token_dict_gftokens_gc95M.pkl` | Ensembl ID → token ID (incl. `<pad>`, `<cls>`, `<eos>`) | Vocabulary; source of special-token IDs |
| `gene_median_dict_gftokens_gc95M.pkl` | Ensembl ID → median expression | Normalization factors for rank encoding |
| `ensembl_mapping_dict_gc95M.pkl` | Ensembl ID → collapsed Ensembl ID | Gene-ID collapse during `sum_ensembl_ids` |

Sources: [pp/\_\_init\_\_.py](perturbgen/pp/__init__.py#L1-L7), [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L293-L305), [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L8-L11)

## On-Disk Directory Contract for Perturbation Datasets

`GF_tokenisation.py` materializes a fully self-describing directory tree under `{TOKENIZED_DIR}/{dataset}/` (by default `ROOT/T_perturb/tokenized_data/`). All layout names are parameterized by a **gene-filtering suffix** — `{n_hvg}_{gene_filtering_mode}` (e.g. `2000_hvg`) or `all` — so that multiple tokenization variants of the same dataset coexist side by side without collision.

```text
T_perturb/tokenized_data/{dataset}/
├── token_id_to_genename_{suffix}.pkl        # token ID → gene name (decoder label space)
├── tokenid_to_rowid_{suffix}.pkl            # token ID → compact row ID (decoder input space)
├── h5ad_pairing_{suffix}/
│   └── {dataset}.h5ad                       # full adata with cell_pairing_index obs column
├── h5ad_pairing_{suffix}_GF_genes/
│   └── {dataset}.h5ad                       # Geneformer-vocabulary-filtered adata (tokenizer input)
├── h5ad_pairing_{suffix}_src/
│   └── {reference_time}.h5ad                # e.g. "Day 00-03.h5ad"
├── h5ad_pairing_{suffix}_tgt/
│   └── {1..n}_{time_point}.h5ad             # enumerated target time points
├── dataset_{suffix}/
│   └── {dataset}.dataset                    # full tokenized corpus (pre-pairing)
├── dataset_{suffix}_src/
│   └── {reference_time}.dataset             # source-state cells
└── dataset_{suffix}_tgt/
    └── {1..n}_{time_point}.dataset          # target-state cells, paired to src
```

Sources: [GF_tokenisation.py](perturbgen/pp/GF_tokenisation.py#L220-L224), [GF_tokenisation.py](perturbgen/pp/GF_tokenisation.py#L301-L330), [GF_tokenisation.py](perturbgen/pp/GF_tokenisation.py#L408-L429), [GF_tokenisation.py](perturbgen/pp/GF_tokenisation.py#L498-L528)

Two asymmetries in the split layout are load-bearing. First, the **source dataset keeps raw Geneformer token IDs** when `src_mode='Geneformer'` — the comment in the code states Geneformer needs the initial token IDs to extract correct embeddings — whereas **target datasets are always written from the row-ID-mapped dataset** produced by `dataset.map(map_input_ids_to_row_id, ...)`. Second, when `src_mode='Transformer'`, the row-ID-mapped source is instead written into an `h5ad_pairing_{suffix}_src_transformer` directory. Time-point pairing itself (`pairing_src_to_tgt_cells` over `time_obs` with a `reference_time` control state) is detailed in [Cell Pairing and Data Curation](14-cell-pairing-and-data-curation).

Sources: [GF_tokenisation.py](perturbgen/pp/GF_tokenisation.py#L482-L528)

> [!TIP]
> The target enumeration is a parsing contract, not cosmetic decoration: `read_dataset_files` derives the time-step key from `filename[0]` (`f'tgt_dataset_t{filename[0]}'`), so the leading digit in `1_Day 06-09.dataset` becomes the `t` in `tgt_dataset_t1`. Renaming or re-prefixing target files silently corrupts time-step assignment at training time — treat the enumeration digits as immutable.

Sources: [utils.py](perturbgen/src/utils.py#L86-L100)

The full layout-generation flow, from raw `h5ad` to the paired `_src`/`_tgt` split:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Raw h5ad (--h5ad_path)"] --> B["Preprocess: HVG / DEG / all filtering,\nmito-ribo removal, counts layer"]
    B --> C["Write token_id_to_genename_{suffix}.pkl\n+ h5ad_pairing_{suffix}/{dataset}.h5ad"]
    C --> D["Filter to GF vocabulary\n(h5ad_pairing_{suffix}_GF_genes/)"]
    D --> E["tokenid_mapping →\ntokenid_to_rowid_{suffix}.pkl"]
    E --> F["TranscriptomeTokenizer.tokenize_data\n→ dataset_{suffix}/{dataset}.dataset"]
    F --> G["dataset.map(map_input_ids_to_row_id)\n= dataset_mapped"]
    H["pairing_src_to_tgt_cells\n(per time point index lists)"] --> I
    G --> I{"time_point == reference_time?"}
    I -- yes --> J["dataset_{suffix}_src/\n{reference_time}.dataset\n(Geneformer IDs preserved)"]
    I -- no, n-th --> K["dataset_{suffix}_tgt/\n{n}_{time_point}.dataset\n(row-ID space)"]
```

Sources: [GF_tokenisation.py](perturbgen/pp/GF_tokenisation.py#L401-L459), [GF_tokenisation.py](perturbgen/pp/GF_tokenisation.py#L482-L528)

## Path Conventions and CLI Wiring

`configs/paths.py` defines the layout's root constants and **creates the directories at import time** (`mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`), so any module importing `TOKENIZED_DIR` triggers directory materialization. The file also documents the expected workspace shape (`T_perturb/` containing `data/`, `perturbgen/`, `res/`, `tokenized_data/`) and pins the pretrained encoder checkpoint path shipped in `pretraining_cohort/`.

| Constant | Resolved value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ROOT` | 3 levels above `paths.py` | Workspace root (`os.chdir(ROOT)` in entry points) |
| `DATA_DIR` | `ROOT/data` | Raw/intermediate h5ad inputs |
| `TOKENIZED_DIR` | `ROOT/T_perturb/tokenized_data` | Root of all `.dataset`/`.pkl` layout trees |
| `RESULTS_DIR` | `ROOT/T_perturb/res` | Experiment outputs |
| `GENE_MEDIAN_PATH` / `TOKEN_DICT_PATH` / `GENE_MAPPING_PATH` | `REPO_DIR/perturbgen/pp/*.pkl` | Default vocabulary assets |

Sources: [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L1-L35)

`train.py`'s argument defaults point directly at this layout and double as executable documentation of the naming contract: `--src_dataset ./T_perturb/tokenized_data/eb/dataset_hvg_src/Day 00-03.dataset`, `--tgt_dataset_folder ./T_perturb/tokenized_data/eb/dataset_hvg_tgt`, with the h5ad counterparts under `h5ad_pairing_hvg_{src,tgt}`. The `--tokenid_to_rowid_path` argument additionally implements a **derivation heuristic**: if omitted, it is derived from `--mapping_dict_path` by replacing the substring `token_id_to_genename` with `tokenid_to_rowid` — exactly the naming convention the layout guarantees — and fails loudly if the heuristic cannot apply. Note that the default example paths use the bare suffix `hvg` while the generator emits `{n_hvg}_{mode}`; when wiring runs manually, the suffix you pass must match what `GF_tokenisation.py` actually produced.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L106-L145), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L31-L57), [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L19-L34)

## From Disk to Batch: Consumption Contracts

At training time the layout is consumed in three hops. `read_dataset_files(directory, file_type)` scans a `_tgt` folder and keys each entry as `tgt_dataset_t{filename[0]}` (h5ad files become `tgt_h5ad_t{n}`), yielding the `DatasetDict` shape the datamodule expects. `PerturbGenDataset` then holds a `src_dataset` plus one `tgt_dataset_t{t}` per modeled time point, applies splits by `select(split_indices)` (index-aligned across src, tgt, counts, and conditions), computes inverse-frequency label weights from metadata columns (`sampling_keys`) for the `WeightedRandomSampler`, and asserts src/tgt length alignment.

Sources: [utils.py](perturbgen/src/utils.py#L86-L100), [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L31-L84), [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L113-L152), [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L231-L293)

The final hop is `collate`, which converts the Arrow records into padded tensors while enforcing the special-token protocol in the opposite direction of tokenization: source sequences are padded with `<pad>` to the batch's dynamic maximum via `pad_tensor_list` (bounded by `max_len=2048`), whereas **target sequences have `<cls>` and `<eos>` explicitly filtered out** (by ID, not by position — the code does not assume CLS is first) before length re-computation. Count matrices (dense or CSR) are densified once per sample and reused to derive size factors (`tgt_counts.sum(axis=1)`), producing the complete batch dictionary below.

| Batch key | Producer logic | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `src_input_ids`, `src_length` | `pad_tensor_list` with `<pad>` ID, dynamic batch max | Padded source token sequences |
| `src_counts` | CSR densify + `torch.cat` | Raw source count matrix |
| `batch`, `combined_batch` | condition encodings | Categorical condition tensors |
| `tgt_input_ids_t{t}`, `tgt_length_t{t}` | `<cls>`/`<eos>` stripped by ID | Row-space target sequences |
| `tgt_counts_t{t}`, `tgt_size_factor_t{t}` | one densify, sum along axis | Target counts + library size factors |

Sources: [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L331-L399), [gf_utils.py](perturbgen/src/gf_utils.py#L35-L62), [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L295-L313)

The complete interaction between layout assets and the training stack:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Disk["Tokenized layout on disk"]
        P1["tokenid_to_rowid_{suffix}.pkl"]
        D1["dataset_{suffix}_src/*.dataset\n(Geneformer ID space)"]
        D2["dataset_{suffix}_tgt/{n}_*.dataset\n(row-ID space)"]
        A1["h5ad_pairing_{suffix}_{src,tgt}/*.h5ad"]
    end
    subgraph Loader["Training ingestion"]
        U["read_dataset_files\nkeys: tgt_dataset_t{filename[0]}"]
        DS["PerturbGenDataset\nselect(split_indices),\nlabel weights from sampling_keys"]
        DM["PerturbGenDataModule.collate\n<pad> pad src / strip <cls>,<eos> tgt /\nsize factors"]
    end
    T["token_dict_gftokens_gc95M.pkl\n(perturbgen/pp/)"] --> DM
    D1 --> DS
    D2 --> U --> DS
    A1 --> DS
    P1 --> DM
    DS --> DM --> B["Batch: src_input_ids,\ntgt_input_ids_t{t},\ntgt_size_factor_t{t}, conditions"]
```

Sources: [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L175-L226), [utils.py](perturbgen/src/utils.py#L86-L100), [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L331-L399), [pp/\_\_init\_\_.py](perturbgen/pp/__init__.py#L1-L7)

For the pretraining cohort, the layout is simpler — one flat `{file_prefix}.dataset` per harmonized h5ad written into a single output directory — since masked pretraining consumes cells without src/tgt pairing. The pairing split described above applies specifically to perturbation fine-tuning datasets.

Sources: [tokenization.py](pretraining_cohort/tokenization/tokenization.py#L29-L42)

## Where to Go Next

To understand *why* sequences are rank-encoded and how `<cls>`/`<eos>` interact with the encoder, continue to [Geneformer-Style Gene Tokenization](9-geneformer-style-gene-tokenization) and [Time-Aware Positional Encoding](8-time-aware-positional-encoding). For how cell pairings determine which cells land in `_src` versus `_tgt`, see [Cell Pairing and Data Curation](14-cell-pairing-and-data-curation); for the upstream harmonized h5ad inputs this layout consumes, see [Pretraining Cohort Harmonization Pipeline](15-pretraining-cohort-harmonization-pipeline). The resolution mechanics of `ROOT` and the checkpoint constants are expanded in [Configuration System and Path Management](17-configuration-system-and-path-management), and the end-to-end invocation of this layout in practice is covered in [CLI Command Reference](22-cli-command-reference).

# Configuration System and Path Management



PerturbGen deliberately avoids a monolithic configuration framework such as Hydra. Instead, it distributes configuration across three cooperating layers: a **static path registry** compiled into Python at import time, a **CLI argument layer** with environment-variable fallbacks, and **two YAML config families** consumed by different entry points. Understanding how these layers anchor paths to different roots is essential before launching training, sweeps, or perturbation job arrays, because a file path that resolves correctly in one context may silently point elsewhere in another.

## Architecture Overview: Three Path Anchors

The configuration system resolves paths through three distinct anchoring strategies, each serving a different mobility requirement. The static registry anchors to the module file location (immune to working-directory changes), the runtime layer re-anchors the process working directory to the repository parent, and the shell layer anchors to cluster-specific absolute paths. All three converge on the same workspace convention: a `T_perturb/` directory sitting beside the cloned repository.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph static["Layer 1: Static Registry (__file__-anchored)"]
        PP["perturbgen/configs/paths.py<br/>ROOT = parents[3]<br/>REPO_DIR = parents[2]"]
        INIT["configs/__init__.py<br/>re-exports all symbols"]
    end

    subgraph runtime["Layer 2: Runtime Anchoring (cwd-anchored)"]
        TRAIN["train.py<br/>os.chdir(ROOT)"]
        VALP["Perturb/val.py<br/>os.chdir(ROOT)"]
    end

    subgraph yaml["Layer 3: YAML Config Families"]
        SWEEP["configs/sweep/*.yaml<br/>W&B sweep schema"]
        EVAL["configs/eval/&lt;cohort&gt;/*.yaml<br/>data/trainer/datamodule/model"]
        PRE["preprocessing/config_am74.yaml<br/>flat key-value"]
    end

    subgraph shell["Layer 4: Shell Orchestration"]
        LSF["batch_job_script/*.sh<br/>BSUB directives + WANDB_DIR"]
        AGENT["run_sweep.sh<br/>wandb agent"]
        SED["sed s/&#123;&#123;PERTURBED_GENE&#125;&#125;/.../g"]
    end

    PP --> INIT
    INIT --> TRAIN
    INIT --> VALP
    PP -->|"ENCODER_CKPT_PATH default"| TRAIN
    AGENT -->|"reads sweep YAML, launches"| SWEEP
    SWEEP -->|"program: → train.py"| TRAIN
    LSF -->|"--config tmp.yaml"| VALP
    SED -->|"templates"| EVAL
    EVAL -->|"yaml.safe_load"| VALP
    TRAIN -.->|"relative paths resolve<br/>against ROOT after chdir"| WS["ROOT/T_perturb/<br/>tokenized_data/, res/, logs/"]
    VALP -.-> WS
```

The registry is the only layer that survives arbitrary working directories; everything else depends on the `chdir` or on absolute cluster paths written directly into YAML files.

Sources: [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L1-L35), [__init__.py](perturbgen/configs/__init__.py#L1-L13), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L15-L28), [val.py](perturbgen/Perturb/val.py#L13-L24), [mask_src_inference_perturbation_jobarray.yaml](perturbgen/configs/eval/HSPC/mask_src_inference_perturbation_jobarray.yaml#L1-L59), [sweep-hspc-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-hspc-masking.yaml#L1-L62)

## The Static Path Registry: `configs/paths.py`

The registry resolves every path from the module's own file location using `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N]`, which makes it immune to working-directory changes. Two anchor levels are defined: `ROOT` (three levels up — the directory *containing* the cloned repository) and `REPO_DIR` (two levels up — the repository itself). From these, two groups of paths derive: **shipped defaults** bundled with the repository (the tokenization pickles in `perturbgen/pp/` and the pretrained encoder checkpoint in `pretraining_cohort/`), and **workspace paths** under `ROOT/T_perturb/` where generated data, results, and tokenized datasets live.

| Symbol | Value | Anchored to | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ROOT` | `parents[3]` | Directory containing the repo | Workspace root for data/res outputs |
| `REPO_DIR` | `parents[2]` | The repository itself | Locating shipped assets |
| `PP_DIR` | `REPO_DIR/perturbgen/pp` | Repository | Preprocessing asset bundle |
| `GENE_MEDIAN_PATH` | `PP_DIR/gene_median_dict_gftokens_gc95M.pkl` | Repository | Gene median expression values |
| `TOKEN_DICT_PATH` | `PP_DIR/token_dict_gftokens_gc95M.pkl` | Repository | Token vocabulary |
| `GENE_MAPPING_PATH` | `PP_DIR/ensembl_mapping_dict_gc95M.pkl` | Repository | Ensembl ID mapping |
| `ENCODER_CKPT_PATH` | `REPO_DIR/pretraining_cohort/<timestamped>.ckpt` | Repository | Shipped pretrained encoder |
| `PROJECT_DIR` | `ROOT/T_perturb` | Workspace | Project namespace |
| `DATA_DIR` | `ROOT/data` | Workspace | Raw data landing zone |
| `RESULTS_DIR` | `PROJECT_DIR/res` | Workspace | Run outputs |
| `TOKENIZED_DIR` | `PROJECT_DIR/tokenized_data` | Workspace | Tokenized dataset layout |

Sources: [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L3-L16), [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L25-L30)

The registry has **two import-time side effects** that intermediate developers must be aware of. First, the three workspace directories are created unconditionally at import (`mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`), meaning merely importing `perturbgen.configs` writes to the filesystem beside the repository — this is what guarantees the workspace skeleton exists before any entry point runs. Second, because `ROOT` assumes the `repo-and-workspace-siblings` layout documented in the file's comment block (`T_perturb/` beside `perturbgen/`), cloning the repo into an unexpected nesting depth will resolve `ROOT` to the wrong directory with no error at import time. The registry is re-exported through `configs/__init__.py`, so downstream code imports once with `from perturbgen.configs import ROOT, ENCODER_CKPT_PATH` rather than reaching into `paths` directly.

Sources: [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L17-L35), [__init__.py](perturbgen/configs/__init__.py#L1-L13)

## Working-Directory Anchoring: The `os.chdir(ROOT)` Contract

Both major entry points — `train.py` and `Perturb/val.py` — execute `os.chdir(ROOT)` at **module level** (not inside `main()`), printing the resulting working directory for traceability. This is the load-bearing trick that makes relative paths work: every path written as `./T_perturb/...` or `T_perturb/...` in CLI defaults and YAML configs resolves against `ROOT` regardless of where Python was launched. The practical consequence is that the entire configuration surface is only coherent *because* of this side effect; running either module as a library import in a notebook (the in-process API path) will also relocate the notebook's working directory.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Shell as Shell / wandb agent
    participant Py as train.py module
    participant FS as Filesystem

    Shell->>Py: import (module level)
    Py->>Py: from perturbgen.configs import ROOT, ENCODER_CKPT_PATH
    Note over Py: paths.py mkdirs workspace dirs
    Py->>FS: os.chdir(ROOT)
    Py->>Shell: prints "Current working directory: ..."
    Shell->>Py: main(argv) → get_args()
    Note over Py: argparse defaults like ./T_perturb/...<br/>now resolve relative to ROOT
    Py->>FS: load_from_disk(args.src_dataset)<br/>os.makedirs(log_path)
```

The evaluation entry point applies the identical pattern (`os.chdir(ROOT)` at module scope), so eval YAMLs containing bare `T_perturb/...` relative paths resolve consistently even when the job array script's own `-cwd` points elsewhere. When debugging path failures, always compare the printed working directory against where the config's relative paths actually sit — a mismatch between the two is the root cause of most "file not found" errors in this codebase.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L15-L28), [val.py](perturbgen/Perturb/val.py#L23-L24), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L60-L61)

## CLI Argument Layer: Defaults, Env-Vars, and Path Derivation

`get_args()` in `train.py` defines the full training surface via argparse, and its defaults encode the workspace convention: `--output_dir` points to `./T_perturb/perturbgen/plt/res/cytoimmgen/pbmc_median`, and the four data-path arguments point to EB-dataset defaults under `./T_perturb/tokenized_data/eb/`. These defaults are relative and therefore only meaningful after the `chdir`. The only true environment-variable integration lives in the Weights & Biases arguments: `--wandb_mode`, `--wandb_entity`, and `--wandb_project` each use `os.environ.get('WANDB_MODE', ...)` as their default, so cluster shell scripts control logging behavior without touching the training command line.

| Argument | Default | Resolution anchor |
|---|---|---|
| `--output_dir` | `./T_perturb/perturbgen/plt/res/cytoimmgen/pbmc_median` | cwd (= ROOT post-chdir) |
| `--src_dataset` / `--tgt_dataset_folder` | `./T_perturb/tokenized_data/eb/...` | cwd (= ROOT post-chdir) |
| `--mapping_dict_path` | `None` (required — fails loudly) | caller-provided |
| `--encoder_path` | `str(ENCODER_CKPT_PATH)` | `__file__`-anchored registry |
| `--wandb_mode` | `WANDB_MODE` env var, else `offline` | environment |
| `--wandb_entity` / `--wandb_project` | env vars, else `None` / `perturbgen` | environment |

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L81-L135), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L168-L194), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L291-L296)

One path is never given directly but *derived*: the token-to-row mapping. `_resolve_tokenid_to_rowid_path()` implements a naming-convention heuristic — if `--tokenid_to_rowid_path` is omitted, the code rewrites `token_id_to_genename` to `tokenid_to_rowid` inside the `--mapping_dict_path` string. Critically, the heuristic **fails loudly** rather than silently: if the mapping path does not contain the expected substring, it raises a `ValueError` with an actionable message, and if neither argument is given it refuses to proceed. This design trades convenience for safety — follow the `tokenid_to_rowid` / `token_id_to_genename` file-pair naming convention from tokenization, or pass both paths explicitly.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L31-L57)

## YAML Config Family 1: W&B Sweep Configs

The files in `configs/sweep/` follow the **Weights & Biases sweep schema**, not a framework-internal format. Three keys identify them as W&B configs: `method: grid` (search strategy), `metric: {goal, name}` (the monitored objective, here `val/perplexity_epoch`), and `program:` — the absolute path to `train.py` that `wandb agent` will execute. The `parameters:` block mixes two value shapes: `value:` pins a fixed setting (data paths, `train_mode`, epochs), while `values:` lists the grid axes (e.g., `num_layers: [4, 6]` crossed with three `cellgen_lr` × three `cellgen_wd` values → 18 runs per sweep file). Because the sweep parameters are injected as CLI flags into `train.py`, every key here must match an argparse argument name exactly.

| Key | Role | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | W&B search strategy | `grid` |
| `metric.name` | Objective monitored | `val/perplexity_epoch` |
| `parameters.<arg>.value` | Fixed CLI value | `train_mode: masking` |
| `parameters.<arg>.values` | Grid axis | `cellgen_lr: [0.0001, 0.00001, 0.001]` |
| `program` | Entry point executed by the agent | absolute cluster path to `train.py` |
| `project` | W&B project receiving runs | `ttransformer_sweep` |

The sweep configs hardcode both absolute cluster paths (in `program:`) and relative workspace paths (in data parameters), which means a sweep file is tied to both a specific cluster mount and the `chdir`-anchored workspace layout. Eight ready-made sweep files cover the four cohorts (HSPC, LPS, EB, cytoimmgen) × the two training modes (masking, count), plus a generation sweep.

Sources: [sweep-hspc-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-hspc-masking.yaml#L1-L62), [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L20-L25)

## YAML Config Family 2: Nested Eval Configs with Template Placeholders

Evaluation configs use a **four-section nested schema** (`data:`, `trainer:`, `datamodule:`, `model:`) parsed by `Perturb/val.py` via `yaml.safe_load`. Unlike sweeps, these are consumed internally: `val.py` takes a single `--config` argument whose default points at an HSPC perturbation config, then reads dataset paths from `config['data']`, model and perturbation settings from `config['trainer']`, and precision from `config['model']`. The HSPC job-array variant demonstrates the system's one templating mechanism: the `genes_to_perturb` list contains the literal placeholder `{{PERTURBED_GENE}}`, which is substituted per job before parsing.

| Section | Contents | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|
| `data:` | src/tgt dataset + adata paths, optional `perturb_genes_file` | val.py data loading |
| `trainer:` | vocab size, architecture dims, `perturbation_mode`, `genes_to_perturb`, `output_dir`, checkpoint path | PerturberTrainer construction |
| `datamodule:` | batch size, workers, `max_len`, `var_list` | PerturbGenDataModule |
| `model:` | `precision`, `ckpt_masking_path` | Lightning Trainer precision strategy |

Sources: [mask_src_inference_perturbation_jobarray.yaml](perturbgen/configs/eval/HSPC/mask_src_inference_perturbation_jobarray.yaml#L1-L59), [val.py](perturbgen/Perturb/val.py#L31-L52), [val.py](perturbgen/Perturb/val.py#L128-L146)

## Template-Based Config Generation in Job Arrays

The `{{PERTURBED_GENE}}` placeholder is resolved by shell tooling, not Python. The HSPC job-array script reads gene *N* (from `LSB_JOBINDEX`) out of a gene list file, applies `sed "s/{{PERTURBED_GENE}}/${PERTURBED_GENE}/g"` to write a per-job temporary YAML, invokes `val.py --config $TMP_CONFIG_PATH`, and registers a `trap` on exit to delete the temporary file. This produces one config per perturbed gene without storing hundreds of YAML files — the config files in the repository are templates, and the materialized variants are ephemeral artifacts of the batch system.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["LSB job array<br/>index 1..N"] --> B["sed -n INDEXp<br/>test_100M.txt"]
    B --> C{"gene empty?"}
    C -->|yes| X["exit 1 with error"]
    C -->|no| D["sed s/&#123;&#123;PERTURBED_GENE&#125;&#125;/GENE/g<br/>→ TMP_CONFIG yaml"]
    D --> E["val.py --config TMP"]
    E --> F{"output file for<br/>gene already exists?"}
    F -->|yes| G["skip gene<br/>(idempotent resume)"]
    F -->|no| H["run perturbation inference"]
    H --> I["trap EXIT: rm TMP_CONFIG"]
```

Evaluation is additionally **idempotent at the config level**: `val.py` lists the contents of `config['trainer']['output_dir']`, regex-matches filenames against each pending gene (`adata_g<gene>_ssrc`), and removes already-completed genes from the work list before running. Combined with the per-job templating, this makes re-submitting an interrupted job array safe — completed perturbations are skipped automatically.

Sources: [3_perturb_job_array.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array.sh#L24-L44), [val.py](perturbgen/Perturb/val.py#L102-L127)

## Self-Describing Artifact Naming

Configuration state is also encoded *into* artifact names, so results remain interpretable without side-channel metadata. `train.py` composes a timestamped `run_id` (`%Y%m%d_%H%M_cellgen`) plus a hyperparameter signature into every checkpoint filename — masking runs embed `lr`, `wd`, `batch_size`, positional-encoding mode, mask scheduler, predicted timepoints, and seed (e.g., the shipped `20250709_1223_cellgen_train_masking_lr_5e-05_wd_1e-06_batch_64_ptime_pos_sin_m_pow_tp_1-2-3_s_42-epoch=00.ckpt`). The `ENCODER_CKPT_PATH` registry entry demonstrates why: the checkpoint's full provenance is recoverable from its name alone. Checkpoints land in `os.path.join(args.output_dir, 'checkpoints')`, while logs go to `<log_dir>/<run_id>` under the current working directory, and resume behavior dispatches on extension — a `.bin` file is loaded as a raw state dict with `strict=False`, anything else is treated as a Lightning `.ckpt` and passed to `trainer.fit(ckpt_path=...)`.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L574-L602), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L610-L638), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L692-L713), [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L12-L16)

## The Preprocessing Pipeline Config

The pretraining harmonization pipeline uses a deliberately simpler, **flat YAML schema** with absolute cluster paths: `input_dir` and `output_base_dir` define the bronze→silver transformation endpoints, three pickle dictionaries (`dev_stage_map`, `tissue_map`, `disease_map`) provide ontology mappings, and a `gene_filtering:` block points to the non-coding-gene exclusion list and the Ensembl mapping dictionary. There is no `{{...}}` templating, no nesting, and no `chdir` involvement — every path must be absolute, making this config self-contained and portable across job submission directories. The contrast with the eval configs is a useful illustration of the codebase's philosophy: flat schema where the pipeline is a single script, nested schema where many subsystems must be parameterized at once.

Sources: [config_am74.yaml](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/config_am74.yaml#L1-L11)

## Configuration Format Taxonomy: Comparison

| Property | Path registry (`paths.py`) | CLI defaults (`train.py`) | Sweep YAMLs | Eval YAMLs | Preprocessing YAML |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Format | Python module | argparse | W&B sweep schema | Nested YAML (4 sections) | Flat YAML |
| Path anchoring | `__file__` (cwd-independent) | cwd after `chdir(ROOT)` | absolute `program:` + relative params | relative to cwd (= ROOT) | absolute cluster paths |
| Consumer | `from perturbgen.configs import ...` | `main(argv)` | `wandb agent` → launches `train.py` | `Perturb/val.py --config` | `harmonize_bronze_to_silver.py` |
| Templating | none | env-var defaults | none | `{{PERTURBED_GENE}}` via `sed` | none |
| Side effects | mkdir workspace dirs | chdir process cwd | none (W&B runtime) | none | none |
| Portability | portable (repo-relative) | portable (workspace-relative) | cluster-bound | workspace-bound | cluster-bound |

Sources: [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L1-L35), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L60-L135), [sweep-hspc-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-hspc-masking.yaml#L1-L62), [mask_src_inference_perturbation_jobarray.yaml](perturbgen/configs/eval/HSPC/mask_src_inference_perturbation_jobarray.yaml#L1-L59), [config_am74.yaml](pretraining_cohort/preprocessing/config_am74.yaml#L1-L11)

## Practical Failure Modes and Their Root Causes

Three misconfigurations account for most path failures in practice. First, **wrong `ROOT` resolution**: if the repository is nested deeper or shallower than the expected `T_perturb/` sibling layout, `parents[3]` silently points at the wrong tree — the symptom is `chdir` succeeding but all relative paths missing; the fix is to restore the documented sibling layout or edit `paths.py` anchors. Second, **env-var leakage**: `WANDB_MODE` unset defaults runs to `offline`, which is safe for laptops but means sweeps appear to run without logging to the W&B project; cluster scripts like `run_sweep.sh` also redirect artifacts with `export WANDB_DIR=$cwd/wandb`, so wandb files land beside the script's working directory, not inside the repo. Third, **breaking the naming heuristic**: renaming `token_id_to_genename_*.pkl` without its `tokenid_to_rowid_*` twin trips the derivation check — either restore the convention or pass `--tokenid_to_rowid_path` explicitly.

> [!TIP]
> Because `train.py` and `Perturb/val.py` both `chdir` at import time, importing either module inside a long-running notebook session permanently changes the session's working directory. The in-process API accounts for this — but if you import these modules manually, capture any relative paths you care about *before* the import.

> [!TIP]
> The eval YAMLs' `encoder_path` shows the system's escape hatch for infrastructure drift: sweep files and eval configs may carry **different absolute cluster checkpoints**. When reusing a config on a new cluster, audit every absolute path (`program:`, `encoder_path:`, preprocessing YAML entries) — the repository-shipped `ENCODER_CKPT_PATH` is the only path guaranteed to exist after a fresh clone.

Sources: [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L3-L6), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L27-L28), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L168-L194), [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L18-L24), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L31-L57), [mask_src_inference_perturbation_jobarray.yaml](perturbgen/configs/eval/HSPC/mask_src_inference_perturbation_jobarray.yaml#L20-L20)

## Where to Go Next

To see these configs in motion during actual hyperparameter searches, continue with [Hyperparameter Sweeps and Batch Jobs](18-hyperparameter-sweeps-and-batch-jobs), which covers the `wandb agent` workflow and LSF job-array mechanics in depth. For how the paths registered here feed multi-GPU execution, see [Distributed Training with DDP and DeepSpeed](19-distributed-training-with-ddp-and-deepspeed), and for how the W&B arguments configured by environment variables surface in experiment tracking, see [Experiment Tracking with Weights and Biases](20-experiment-tracking-with-weights-and-biases). The workspace directories this system creates (`tokenized_data/`, `res/`) are documented structurally in [Tokenized Dataset Layout](16-tokenized-dataset-layout).

# Hyperparameter Sweeps and Batch Jobs



This page documents the execution-operations layer of PerturbGen: how model training, generation, and in-silico perturbation workloads are scaled across the LSF HPC cluster. The repository provides three complementary orchestration mechanisms — **Weights & Biases sweep agents** for hyperparameter grid search, **numbered sequential batch scripts** for end-to-end dataset pipelines, and **LSF job arrays** for massively parallel per-gene perturbation. All three converge on the same two entry points (`train.py` and `Perturb/val.py`), which is the central design invariant of this layer.

Sources: [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L22-L26), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L60-L68), [Perturb/val.py](perturbgen/Perturb/val.py#L31-L38)

## Orchestration Architecture

The sweep and batch infrastructure forms three independent execution lanes that share the same parameter vocabulary and the same W&B logging substrate. Before reading the diagram: solid boxes are files or commands in the repository, dashed arrows are checkpoint hand-offs between pipeline stages, and the three labeled groups correspond to the three mechanisms detailed in later sections.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph S["Sweep lane — W&B grid search"]
        A["configs/sweep/*.yaml<br/>(grid definition)"] --> B["wandb sweep<br/>registers grid, returns ID"]
        B --> C["run_sweep.sh<br/>(LSF submission)"]
        C --> D["wandb agent<br/>entity/project/sweepID"]
        D --> E["train.py or val.py<br/>one CLI invocation per combo"]
    end
    subgraph P["Pipeline lane — numbered batch scripts"]
        F["1_ GF tokenisation (CPU)"] --> G["2_ masking training"]
        G --> H["3_ count training"]
        H --> I["4_ val / generate"]
    end
    subgraph J["Job-array lane — parallel perturbation"]
        K["gene list + LSF [1-N]%K"] --> L["sed templating<br/>{{PERTURBED_GENE}}"]
        L --> M["Perturb/val.py --config"]
    end
    E --> W["W&B runs<br/>(offline by default)"]
    I --> W
    G -- "ckpt_masking_path" --> H
    H -- "ckpt_count_path" --> I
    M --> R["per-gene output dirs"]
```

The sweep lane is for exploration — it varies learning rates, weight decays, and architecture widths to minimize a validation metric. The pipeline lane is for production — it runs the four canonical stages per dataset with curated, fixed hyperparameters, chaining checkpoints between stages. The job-array lane is for evaluation scale-out — it fans one hand-written perturbation config across thousands of genes. Because all lanes invoke the same Python entry points, a hyperparameter combination discovered in a sweep can be promoted verbatim into a batch script.

Sources: [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L1-L26), [2_run_train_masking_GF_frozen_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/2_run_train_masking_GF_frozen_interpolation.sh#L41-L67), [3_perturb_job_array.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array.sh#L24-L41)

| Mechanism | Launcher | Entry point | Config artifact | Parameter passing | Primary use case |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| W&B sweep | `run_sweep.sh` (LSF) | `program:` field → `train.py` / `val.py` | `perturbgen/configs/sweep/*.yaml` | Agent-generated CLI flags from grid combos | Grid search over LR/WD/architecture |
| Sequential pipeline | Numbered scripts in `batch_job_script/<dataset>/` | `train.py` / `val.py` | Inline CLI flags | Explicit flags per stage | Curated training runs per dataset |
| Job array | `3_perturb_job_array*.sh` (LSF) | `Perturb/val.py --config` | Templated eval YAML | `sed` substitution of `{{PERTURBED_GENE}}` | Per-gene in-silico perturbation at scale |

Sources: [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L20-L26), [3_run_train_count_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/3_run_train_count_interpolation.sh#L37-L42), [3_perturb_job_array.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array.sh#L29-L44), [sweep-lps-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml#L73-L74)

## W&B Sweep Configuration Anatomy

Each file in `perturbgen/configs/sweep/` follows the native W&B sweep schema, extended with a `program` key that tells the agent which Python script to drive. The schema has a strict two-tier structure: global search properties (`method`, `metric`, `name`), and a `parameters` block whose keys must exactly match the argparse flag names of the target program, minus the leading `--`.

Sources: [sweep-lps-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml#L1-L74), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L60-L341)

| Field | Role | Example from `sweep-lps-masking.yaml` |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | Search strategy | `grid` (line 2) |
| `metric.name` / `metric.goal` | Sweep objective | `val/perplexity_epoch`, `minimize` (lines 3–5) |
| `name` | Sweep display name in W&B UI | `tune_masking_lps` (line 6) |
| `parameters.<key>.value` | **Fixed** parameter — passed identically to every run | `train_mode: 'masking'` (lines 8–9) |
| `parameters.<key>.values` | **Swept** parameter — grid axis; combos form the cartesian product | `d_ff: [32, 64]` (lines 42–43) |
| `program` | Python entry point the agent invokes | `.../perturbgen/train.py` (line 73) |
| `project` | Target W&B project | `ttransformer_sweep` (line 74) |

A critical semantic distinction governs the `parameters` block: `value` pins a parameter, while `values` expands it into a grid axis. Every key declared in the block is transmitted to the program as a CLI flag on every run — fixed values included — so the sweep config is a complete, self-contained argv specification, not a partial override.

> [!TIP]
> The sweep YAML ↔ argparse mapping is a hard contract: a parameter key that does not match a flag in `train.py`'s `get_args()` will make the agent's invocation fail. Note the cautionary example in `sweep-hspc-masking.yaml`, where `num_layers` uses `value: [4, 6]` instead of `values` — under W&B semantics this fixes the parameter to a single list literal rather than expanding it into two grid points.

Sources: [sweep-hspc-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-hspc-masking.yaml#L38-L47), [sweep-lps-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml#L7-L65)

## Sweep Inventory

Eight sweep configs cover the dataset × training-stage matrix. File names encode the dataset and the stage (`masking` = encoder pretraining on masked sequences, `count` = count-decoder fine-tuning, `generate` = sampling-parameter tuning). The `program` field confirms that stage sweeps target `train.py` while generation sweeps target `val.py`.

Sources: [sweep-lps-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml#L73), [sweep-cyto-count.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-cyto-count.yaml#L53), [sweep-generate.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-generate.yaml#L55)

| Config file | Dataset | Stage (from name) | Verified objective | Verified swept axes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sweep-lps-masking.yaml` | LPS | masking | `val/perplexity_epoch` ↓ | `d_ff` [2] × `cellgen_lr` [4] × `cellgen_wd` [3] → **24 runs** |
| `sweep-cyto-count.yaml` | cytoimmgen | count | `val/mse_epoch` ↓ | `count_dropout` [2] × `count_lr` [3] × `batch_size` [2] → **12 runs** |
| `sweep-hspc-masking.yaml` | HSPC | masking | `val/perplexity_epoch` ↓ | `cellgen_lr` [3] × `cellgen_wd` [3] → **9 runs** |
| `sweep-generate.yaml` | cytoimmgen | generation (`val.py`) | `test/emd` ↓ | `mask_scheduler` [3] × `temperature` [4] → **12 runs** |
| `sweep-lps-count.yaml` | LPS | count | — | — |
| `sweep-cyto-masking.yaml` | cytoimmgen | masking | — | — |
| `sweep-eb-count.yaml` | EB | count | — | — |
| `sweep-eb-masking.yaml` | EB | masking | — | — |

Two structural observations from the verified configs: first, the generation sweep is the only one targeting `val.py`, and it tunes **sampling** hyperparameters (`mask_scheduler`, `temperature`) against a distributional metric (`test/emd`) rather than training hyperparameters. Second, sweep configs embed fixed absolute paths to frozen encoder checkpoints (e.g., the `scmaskgit` foundation checkpoint in `encoder_path`), so sweeps fine-tune downstream modules on top of a fixed pretrained encoder.

Sources: [sweep-generate.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-generate.yaml#L7-L54), [sweep-lps-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml#L43-L57), [sweep-cyto-count.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-cyto-count.yaml#L44-L52), [sweep-lps-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml#L48-L49)

## Launching a Sweep on the LSF Cluster

Launching a sweep is a two-artifact workflow: the YAML defines *what* to search, and `run_sweep.sh` defines *where* the agent executes. The script is an LSF job wrapper whose payload is a single `wandb agent` command bound to an entity/project/sweep-ID triple.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S1["1. Edit sweep YAML<br/>fix paths, set grid"] --> S2["2. wandb sweep<br/>configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml"]
    S2 --> S3["3. Copy returned sweep ID<br/>e.g. 42vqfszc"]
    S3 --> S4["4. Paste ID into run_sweep.sh<br/>agent line"]
    S4 --> S5["5. bsub &lt; run_sweep.sh"]
    S5 --> S6["6. Agent pulls combos,<br/>runs train.py per combo"]
    S6 --> S7["7. Monitor objective<br/>val/perplexity_epoch in W&B"]
    S7 --> S8["8. Grid exhausted →<br/>select best checkpoint"]
```

The `run_sweep.sh` resource profile is deliberately heavyweight — 4 exclusive GPUs (`#BSUB -gpu 'mode=exclusive_process:num=4'`), 8 CPU cores, 50 GB RAM on the `gpu-lotfollahi` queue — because the sweep agent serializes full training runs on that allocation. The script performs three setup actions before the payload: loading CUDA 12.1.1 via `module load`, activating the shared conda environment, and exporting `WANDB_DIR=$cwd/wandb` so run artifacts land inside the working directory rather than a home-directory default.

Sources: [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L1-L26)

The agent line itself — `wandb agent lotfollahi/ttransformer_sweep/42vqfszc` — requires a manual paste of the sweep ID returned by the `wandb sweep` registration command (the inline comment `#paste wandb with sweep id` marks this as an intentional manual step). The sweep ID shown corresponds to the LPS masking sweep per the output-file naming (`%J_lps_sweep.out`); when sweeping a different config, both the agent line and the ID must be replaced.

Sources: [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L7-L8), [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L22-L25)

### How the agent reaches the training code

For every grid combination, the agent constructs one CLI invocation of `program` with `--key value` pairs derived from the `parameters` block. This means boolean-typed flags arrive as strings, which `train.py` handles through its `str2bool` converter (used for `--split`, `--context_mode`, `--use_weighted_sampler`). Logging behavior during sweeps is governed by the same flags as interactive use: `--wandb_mode` defaults to the `WANDB_MODE` environment variable, falling back to `offline` — a deliberate safety choice, as the help text notes offline runs "never hang on authentication" on headless compute nodes and can be uploaded later with `wandb sync`.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L153-L179), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L621-L638)

## The Sequential Batch Job Pipeline

The `batch_job_script/` directory implements the four-stage lifecycle per dataset using a numeric-prefix convention that makes the execution order legible from filenames. Stage 1 is CPU-bound data engineering; stages 2–4 are GPU-bound and chain checkpoints forward.

Sources: [1_run_GF_tokenisation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/cytoimmgen/1_run_GF_tokenisation.sh#L1-L42), [4_run_val_generate_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/4_run_val_generate_interpolation.sh#L40-L74)

| Stage prefix | Operation | Entry point | Compute profile | Hands off via |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `1_` | Geneformer-style tokenisation + cell pairing | `pp/GF_tokenisation.py` | CPU queue, 150 GB RAM | Tokenized `.dataset`/`.h5ad` folders |
| `2_` | Masking encoder training | `train.py --train_mode masking` | GPU queue, 2 exclusive GPUs | `--ckpt_masking_path` → stage 3 |
| `3_` | Count decoder training | `train.py --train_mode count` | GPU queue, 2 exclusive GPUs | `--ckpt_count_path` → stage 4 |
| `4_` | Generative validation | `val.py --generate True` | GPU queue, 1 GPU | Downstream analysis |

Sources: [1_run_GF_tokenisation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/cytoimmgen/1_run_GF_tokenisation.sh#L3-L11), [2_run_train_masking_GF_frozen_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/2_run_train_masking_GF_frozen_interpolation.sh#L3-L4), [3_run_train_count_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/3_run_train_count_interpolation.sh#L2-L3), [4_run_val_generate_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/4_run_val_generate_interpolation.sh#L2-L3)

Dataset directories specialize this template:

| Directory | Layout |
|---|---|
| `cytoimmgen/`, `eb/` | `1_` tokenisation + `interpolation/` and `extrapolation/` subdirectories, each holding stages `2_/3_/4_` |
| `lps/` | `1_`, a single `2_` masking script (90 min timepoint), `interpolation/` + `extrapolation/` stage sets, and a standalone `4_perturb.sh` |
| `hspc/` | `1_`, `2.1_/2.2_` masking/count variants (all-TF vs inter-TF timepoints), `2.3_` gene-embedding extraction, `3_perturb*` (single + three job-array variants), `4_` plotting, DEG computation |
| `sko/` | `1_` tokenisation in full and 5k-gene variants, `2_/2.1_` masking + cosine-similarity validation, `3_` count training |

Sources: [repo structure under batch_job_script/](perturbgen/batch_job_script), [2_run_train_masking_Encoder_90min.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/lps/2_run_train_masking_Encoder_90min.sh), [3_perturb_job_array_gpuparallel.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array_gpuparallel.sh#L24)

The interpolation/extrapolation split mirrors the temporal generalization regimes: interpolation scripts pair, for example, EB `Day 00-03` source data with predicted timepoints `--pred_tps 1 2 4` (`--split False`), whereas validation scripts then generate with `--context_tps 1 2 4 --pred_tps 3` for held-out timepoints. For a deeper treatment of these modes see [In Silico Perturbation Modes](10-in-silico-perturbation-modes).

Sources: [2_run_train_masking_GF_frozen_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/2_run_train_masking_GF_frozen_interpolation.sh#L46-L58), [4_run_val_generate_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/4_run_val_generate_interpolation.sh#L61-L62)

### Checkpoint chaining in practice

The EB interpolation sequence demonstrates the hand-off contract concretely. Stage 2 writes checkpoints into `$RES_DIR/$RES_NAME/checkpoints/`; stage 3 then references the selected masking checkpoint explicitly via `--ckpt_masking_path 'T_perturb/res/eb/interpolation/checkpoints/20250828_2043_cellgen_train_masking_..._tp_1-2-4_s_100-epoch=49.ckpt'`; stage 4 references the count checkpoint via `--ckpt_count_path`. Because `train.py`'s `main()` returns the metric-best checkpoint path (`best_model_path`, monitored as `val/perplexity` for masking or `val/mse` for count), callers can select the correct masking checkpoint for the count stage programmatically instead of guessing by epoch.

Sources: [3_run_train_count_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/3_run_train_count_interpolation.sh#L37-L42), [4_run_val_generate_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/4_run_val_generate_interpolation.sh#L46), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L590-L619), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L721-L727)

## Sweep Configs vs Batch Scripts: Same Contract, Two Representations

Because sweeps and batch scripts target the same argparse surface, the identical hyperparameter vocabulary appears in both representations. The comparison below maps fixed values from the LPS masking sweep against the EB interpolation masking script — note how the sweep declares a *distribution* over parameters the batch script pins to single values:

| Parameter | `sweep-lps-masking.yaml` (sweep representation) | EB masking batch script (pinned representation) |
|---|---|---|
| Training mode | `train_mode: value: 'masking'` | `--train_mode masking` |
| Epochs | `epochs: value: 10` | `--epochs 50` |
| Batch size | `batch_size: value: 64` | `--batch_size 64` |
| Learning rate | `cellgen_lr: values: [0.00001, 0.00005, 0.0001, 0.0005]` | `--cellgen_lr 0.001` |
| Weight decay | `cellgen_wd: values: [0.00005, 0.0001, 0.0005]` | `--cellgen_wd 0.0001` |
| Feed-forward dim | `d_ff: values: [32, 64]` | `--d_ff 32` |
| Positional encoding | `pos_encoding_mode: value: 'time_pos_sin'` | `--pos_encoding_mode time_pos_sin` |
| Mask scheduler | `mask_scheduler: value: 'pow'` | `--mask_scheduler 'pow'` |
| Frozen encoder | `encoder_path: value: <foundation ckpt>` | `--encoder_path "<foundation ckpt>"` |

Sources: [sweep-lps-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml#L8-L61), [2_run_train_masking_GF_frozen_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/2_run_train_masking_GF_frozen_interpolation.sh#L42-L67)

This equivalence is the promotion path for sweep results: take the winning combination from the W&B UI, substitute its values into the corresponding `--flags` of a batch script, and resubmit with more epochs for the production run (note the epochs bump from 10 in the sweep to 50 in the pipeline script).

## Job Arrays for Per-Gene Perturbation Sweeps

The HSPC perturbation scripts scale one hand-written evaluation config into hundreds or thousands of isolated runs using LSF job arrays. The mechanism: LSF expands an array notation into indexed jobs, each job reads its gene assignment from a shared gene list file by line number, and `sed` templates that gene into a temporary copy of the YAML config.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    J1["bsub &lt; 3_perturb_job_array.sh"] --> J2["LSF expands [1-6]%4:<br/>6 jobs, max 4 concurrent"]
    J2 --> J3["Per job: sed -n LSB_JOBINDEX p<br/>reads gene N from test_100M.txt"]
    J3 --> J4{"Gene string non-empty?"}
    J4 -- "no" --> J5["Error to stderr, exit 1"]
    J4 -- "yes" --> J6["sed 's/&#123;&#123;PERTURBED_GENE&#125;&#125;/gene/g'<br/>→ temp YAML named gene + LSB_JOBID"]
    J6 --> J7["Perturb/val.py --config temp.yaml"]
    J7 --> J8["trap on EXIT: rm temp.yaml"]
```

Three implementation details make this pattern robust under concurrency. The job-name directive `#BSUB -J hspc_perturb_cluster_[1-6]%4` declares both the array range and the throttling (`%4` = at most four concurrent jobs), with `%I` in the log filenames distinguishing per-index stdout/stderr. The temporary config path embeds `$LSB_JOBID` — the unique LSF job identifier — so simultaneous jobs writing configs for the same gene can never collide. Finally, `trap "rm -f $TMP_CONFIG_PATH" EXIT` guarantees temp-file cleanup even when `val.py` fails, keeping the config directory free of thousands of stale per-gene YAMLs.

Sources: [3_perturb_job_array.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array.sh#L4-L9), [3_perturb_job_array.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array.sh#L24-L44)

The templated config itself is a structured YAML with `data` / `trainer` / `datamodule` / `model` sections; the placeholder sits under `trainer.genes_to_perturb` with `perturbation_mode: 'mask'` and `validation_mode: 'inference'`:

```yaml
perturbation_mode: 'mask'
genes_to_perturb:
  - {{PERTURBED_GENE}}
validation_mode: 'inference'
```

Sources: [mask_src_inference_perturbation_jobarray.yaml](perturbgen/configs/eval/HSPC/mask_src_inference_perturbation_jobarray.yaml#L23-L26)

The scale ceiling is demonstrated by the GPU-parallel variant: `3_perturb_job_array_gpuparallel.sh` requests the `gpu-parallel` queue and declares `#BSUB -J hspc_perturb_cluster_[1-4700]%16` — 4,700 single-GPU jobs throttled to 16 concurrent, drawing genes from `default_rest_genes.txt` instead of the TF-focused list. The array-range constant and the gene-list file must be kept in sync; the empty-gene guard in each script fails fast with a non-zero exit when the job index overshoots the list.

> [!TIP]
> The gene-list + `sed`-template + `$LSB_JOBID`-suffixed temp-file + `trap`-cleanup quartet is a reusable pattern for any embarrassingly parallel config sweep — it converts one YAML into N isolated runs without touching Python code, and is the cluster-native alternative to W&B sweeps when the varied parameter is a data artifact (a gene) rather than a training hyperparameter.

Sources: [3_perturb_job_array_gpuparallel.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array_gpuparallel.sh#L2-L4), [3_perturb_job_array_gpuparallel.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array_gpuparallel.sh#L24-L44), [3_perturb_job_array.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array.sh#L34-L37)

## LSF Directive Reference

All submission scripts share the same BSUB vocabulary. `%J` expands to the LSF job ID and `%I` to the array job index in log paths.

| Directive | Meaning | Representative values |
|---|---|---|
| `-q` | Queue / partition | `gpu-lotfollahi`, `gpu-normal`, `gpu-parallel`, `normal` (CPU), `cpu-interactive` |
