| `-gpu` | GPU allocation mode | `'mode=exclusive_process:num=4'` (sweeps), `num=2` (training), `num=1` (generation/array jobs) |
| `-n` | CPU cores | 4–8 |
| `-G` | Billing group | `team361`, `cellulargenetics-priority` |
| `-cwd` | Working directory at job start | `/lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/kl11/T_perturb/perturbgen` |
| `-o` / `-e` | stdout / stderr capture | `logs/sweep/%J_lps_sweep.out`, `..._%J_%I.err` (arrays) |
| `-M` + `-R` | Memory limit (MB) + resource selection | 20000 (training), 50000 (sweeps/perturb), 150000 (tokenisation) |
| `-J` | Job name; array spec with throttle | `lps_sweep`, `hspc_perturb_cluster_[1-4700]%16` |

Sources: [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L1-L11), [1_run_GF_tokenisation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/cytoimmgen/1_run_GF_tokenisation.sh#L3-L11), [3_perturb_job_array_gpuparallel.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array_gpuparallel.sh#L1-L11), [run_test.sh](perturbgen/run_test.sh#L2-L10)

A companion script, `run_test.sh`, applies the same LSF conventions to the CPU-interactive queue to run the `unittest` test suite on the cluster (`python -m unittest discover .../perturbgen/tests/`), confirming the batch-script pattern covers non-training workloads too. For the test suite itself see [Test and Benchmark Suite](26-test-and-benchmark-suite).

Sources: [run_test.sh](perturbgen/run_test.sh#L20-L24)

## Parameter Flow into the Training Entry Point

`train.py` exposes roughly sixty argparse flags through `get_args()`, grouped as follows. The batch scripts and sweep agents are both clients of this single surface — there is no separate sweep-specific API.

| Group | Representative flags | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pipeline control | `--train_mode`, `--split`, `--splitting_mode`, `--output_dir` | `masking` vs `count`; splits: `random`/`stratified`/`unseen_cond` |
| Data locations | `--src_dataset`, `--tgt_dataset_folder`, `--src_adata`, `--tgt_adata_folder`, `--mapping_dict_path`, `--tokenid_to_rowid_path` | Point at the tokenized layout produced by stage 1 |
| Optimisation (swept axes) | `--cellgen_lr`, `--cellgen_wd`, `--count_lr`, `--count_wd`, `--count_dropout`, `--batch_size`, `--epochs` | The variables sweeps vary |
| Architecture | `--d_model`, `--num_layers`, `--d_ff`, `--pos_encoding_mode`, `--mask_scheduler`, `--encoder`, `--encoder_path` | Encoder checkpoint defaults to the repo-shipped pretrained model |
| Logging | `--wandb_mode`, `--wandb_entity`, `--wandb_project`, `--log_dir` | Each falls back to `WANDB_*` env vars |
| Distributed | `--parallel_distribution`, `--num_node`, `--single_device` | `ddp` (default) or `deepspeed` |
| Generation-time | `--temperature`, `--iterations`, `--n_samples`, `--context_tps` | Consumed by `val.py` in stage 4 |

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L60-L341)

Run identification is fully deterministic from hyperparameters: each run builds a `run_id` from a timestamp, and the checkpoint filename template embeds the training mode, learning rate, weight decay, batch size, positional-encoding mode, mask scheduler, predicted timepoints, and seed — for example `20250828_2043_cellgen_train_masking_lr_0.001_wd_0.0001_batch_64_ptime_pos_sin_m_pow_tp_1-2-4_s_100-epoch=49.ckpt`. On multi-GPU runs (`torch.cuda.device_count() > 1`) a 6-character UUID suffix disambiguates W&B run names across DDP ranks. When `--wandb_mode disabled` is set, the code skips `wandb.init()` entirely by passing `logger=False` to the Lightning Trainer.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L574-L576), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L583-L619), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L622-L638), [3_run_train_count_interpolation.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/eb/interpolation/3_run_train_count_interpolation.sh#L42)

Multi-GPU behavior is automatic: with more than one visible GPU the Trainer selects `devices=-1` and the strategy chosen by `--parallel_distribution` (`DDPStrategy` or `DeepSpeedStrategy` at stage 2); with one GPU or `--single_device True`, it falls back to a notebook-safe single-device strategy. The in-process API sets `--single_device` because multi-process strategies cannot launch inside an interactive Jupyter kernel — the batch scripts are the supported route to multi-GPU. Distribution internals are covered in [Distributed Training with DDP and DeepSpeed](19-distributed-training-with-ddp-and-deepspeed); W&B tracking specifics in [Experiment Tracking with Weights and Biases](20-experiment-tracking-with-weights-and-biases).

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L656-L688), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L148-L152)

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueError: Dataset ... has out of bounds token ids` | Auto-detected `max_len` / vocab smaller than the tokenized data | Pass explicit `--max_len` / `--tgt_vocab_size` overrides (they are offsets applied before the model adds condition/+50 and +100 margins) |
| `Could not derive the tokenid_to_rowid path from --mapping_dict_path` | Mapping pickle does not follow the `token_id_to_genename` naming convention | Pass `--tokenid_to_rowid_path` explicitly |
| Sweep agent launches nothing, or runs the wrong config | Stale sweep ID hardcoded in `run_sweep.sh` | Re-run `wandb sweep` on your edited YAML and paste the fresh ID into the agent line |
| `wandb.init()` hangs on a compute node | Online-mode authentication on a headless host | Keep the default offline mode; upload later with `wandb sync`, or set `--wandb_mode disabled` |
| Duplicate/missing configs during job arrays | Concurrent array jobs overwriting shared files | Keep the `$LSB_JOBID` suffix in temp config names and the `trap ... EXIT` cleanup |
| Array job fails immediately with "does not correspond to a valid gene" | `LSB_JOBINDEX` exceeds gene-list length | Align the `[1-N]` array range with the gene-list line count |
| DDP/DeepSpeed fails when training from a notebook | Multi-process strategies cannot spawn inside an interactive kernel | Set `--single_device True` (the in-process API does this); use batch scripts for multi-GPU |

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L31-L57), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L368-L392), [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L23-L25), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L168-L179), [3_perturb_job_array.sh](perturbgen/batch_job_script/hspc/3_perturb_job_array.sh#L30-L44), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L666-L674)

Note that `train.py` mutates the process working directory at import time (`os.chdir(ROOT)`, where `ROOT` is derived from the config package location) and auto-creates the `T_perturb/res` and `T_perturb/tokenized_data` layout — so relative paths inside sweep YAMLs and batch scripts resolve against that root regardless of where LSF starts the job. Path derivation details are covered in [Configuration System and Path Management](17-configuration-system-and-path-management).

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L27-L28), [configs/paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L3-L35)

## Where to Go Next

The natural reading progression from this page: [Configuration System and Path Management](17-configuration-system-and-path-management) explains the `ROOT`/`ENCODER_CKPT_PATH` defaults that batch scripts rely on; [Experiment Tracking with Weights and Biases](20-experiment-tracking-with-weights-and-biases) details what the sweep agent's runs record; [Distributed Training with DDP and DeepSpeed](19-distributed-training-with-ddp-and-deepspeed) covers the strategy layer selected by `--parallel_distribution`; [Tokenized Dataset Layout](16-tokenized-dataset-layout) describes the artifacts stage-1 jobs produce; [In Silico Perturbation Modes](10-in-silico-perturbation-modes) explains what the job-array scripts execute; and the complete flag inventory lives in [CLI Command Reference](22-cli-command-reference).

# Distributed Training with DDP and DeepSpeed



PerturbGen's training workloads — a 107M-parameter masked generative encoder plus a count decoder — are trained with PyTorch Lightning's strategy abstraction, which lets the same training script transparently scale from a single GPU to multi-GPU and multi-node clusters. This page documents the two distributed backends exposed by the repository (**DDP** and **DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 2**), the exact strategy-selection logic embedded in `perturbgen/train.py`, the batch-size arithmetic that keeps the global batch invariant across device counts, and the operational launch path via LSF/BSUB batch scripts used in production cohorts.

## Architectural Position of Distributed Training

Distributed training in PerturbGen is not a separate subsystem — it is a **strategy selection layer** injected into the Lightning `Trainer` at the end of `main()` in `train.py`. Both the fine-tuning stack (`perturbgen/`) and the encoder pretraining stack (`scmaskgit/`) follow the same decomposition: a `LightningModule` (`PerturbGenTrainer` / `CellGenTrainer`), a `LightningDataModule` (`PerturbGenDataModule` / `CellGenDataModule`), and a strategy object passed to `pl.Trainer`. The strategy is the only component that varies between DDP and DeepSpeed; gradient synchronization, process spawning, and optimizer state sharding are fully delegated to Lightning.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Launch["Launch Layer"]
        LSF["LSF/BSUB batch scripts<br/>batch_job_script/*"] --> CLI["CLI entry<br/>pg train-mask / train.py main()"]
    end
    subgraph Orchestration["Orchestration Layer"]
        CLI --> ARGS["get_args()<br/>--parallel_distribution {ddp, deepspeed}<br/>--num_node, --single_device"]
        ARGS --> SELECT{"multi-GPU<br/>available?"}
        SELECT -->|<=1 GPU or single_device| AUTO["strategy='auto'<br/>devices=1"]
        SELECT -->|>1 GPU| STRAT["parallel_comp_strategy"]
        STRAT -->|ddp| DDP["DDPStrategy<br/>find_unused_parameters=False"]
        STRAT -->|deepspeed| DS["DeepSpeedStrategy<br/>stage=2"]
    end
    subgraph Modules["Device-Replicated Modules"]
        AUTO & DDP & DS --> TRAINER["pl.Trainer<br/>accelerator, devices, num_nodes, strategy"]
        TRAINER --> LM["PerturbGenTrainer<br/>LightningModule"]
        TRAINER --> DM["PerturbGenDataModule<br/>per-GPU batch slicing"]
    end
```

The pretraining stack in `scmaskgit/train.py` follows an identical pattern but is **DDP-only**: its import line leaves `DeepSpeedStrategy` commented out, and it hard-codes `DDPStrategy(find_unused_parameters=True)` with `precision='bf16-mixed'` in the Trainer. This reflects the historical split: the frozen Geneformer-style encoder is pretrained once with DDP + bf16 mixed precision, then fine-tuned within PerturbGen where DeepSpeed becomes available as an option.

Sources: [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L13-L14), [scmaskgit/train.py](/scmaskgit/train.py#L16-L17), [Model/trainer.py](/perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L75-L127)

## Strategy Selection Logic

The entire distributed configuration converges on one CLI argument and one guard condition. `--parallel_distribution` accepts `ddp` or `deepspeed` (default `ddp`), but the choice only takes effect when more than one CUDA device is visible; otherwise the code deliberately degrades to Lightning's `auto` strategy on a single device.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["main() invoked"] --> B{"--single_device<br/>OR cuda.device_count() <= 1?"}
    B -->|Yes| C["devices = 1<br/>strategy = 'auto'"]
    B -->|No| D{"--parallel_distribution"}
    D -->|deepspeed| E["DeepSpeedStrategy(stage=2)"]
    D -->|ddp| F["DDPStrategy<br/>find_unused_parameters=False"]
    E --> G["devices = -1<br/>(all visible GPUs)"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["pl.Trainer(\n  accelerator='gpu',\n  num_nodes=args.num_node,\n  strategy=strategy\n)"]
    H --> I["trainer.fit(module, datamodule)"]
```

The two strategy constructors differ in one consequential flag. The fine-tuning stack uses `find_unused_parameters=False` — the PerturbGen model's parameters all participate in every forward pass under the masking objective, so disabling the unused-parameter scan removes DDP's overhead. The pretraining stack in `scmaskgit/train.py` uses `find_unused_parameters=True`, tolerating frozen or conditionally-executed encoder components during foundation-model training. This asymmetry is deliberate and should be preserved when extending either stack.

| Aspect | `perturbgen/train.py` | `scmaskgit/train.py` |
|---|---|---|
| Available strategies | DDP + DeepSpeed (stage 2) | DDP only (DeepSpeed commented out) |
| `find_unused_parameters` | `False` | `True` |
| Precision | Managed via `set_float32_matmul_precision` on A100/H100 | `precision='bf16-mixed'` in Trainer |
| Device selection | `devices=1` fallback, else `devices=-1` | `devices=-1` if CUDA else `0` |
| Multi-GPU guard | `device_count() > 1` and not `--single_device` | `device_count() > 1` else `'auto'` |

Sources: [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L656-L688), [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L69-L74), [scmaskgit/train.py](/scmaskgit/train.py#L417-L432), [Model/trainer.py](/perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L49-L58)

## DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 2 Configuration

Selecting `--parallel_distribution deepspeed` instantiates `DeepSpeedStrategy(stage=2)`. At ZeRO stage 2, **optimizer states and gradients are partitioned across data-parallel ranks** while parameters remain replicated on every GPU — a memory/communication trade-off suited to PerturbGen's 768-dimensional, ~25k-vocabulary transformer, where parameter replication is affordable but Adam's first/second moment buffers double the per-GPU footprint. No external `deepspeed_config` JSON is committed to the repository; the strategy relies on Lightning's defaults for everything beyond the stage parameter.

Two secondary artifacts confirm the DeepSpeed integration path. First, `scmaskgit/train.py` retains a commented-out import of `convert_zero_checkpoint_to_fp32_state_dict` — the standard utility for converting ZeRO-sharded checkpoints into a single fp32 file loadable outside DeepSpeed ranks — indicating the conversion step is required after stage-2 runs. Second, `perturbgen/tests/benchmark_fused_adam.py` microbenchmarks fused versus non-fused Adam `step()` latency using production shapes (`vocab=25000`, `d_model=768`), quantifying exactly the optimizer-step savings that motivate ZeRO's fused-optimizer path on A100/H100-class hardware.

| ZeRO Stage | Parameter Sharding | Gradient Sharding | Optimizer State Sharding | Relevance Here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | Not used |
| **2** (selected) | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | `DeepSpeedStrategy(stage=2)` in train.py |
| 3 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Not exposed; checkpoint conversion mandatory |

Sources: [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L659-L662), [scmaskgit/train.py](/scmaskgit/train.py#L32-L34), [benchmark_fused_adam.py](/perturbgen/tests/benchmark_fused_adam.py#L1-L7)

## Global Batch Size Invariance

PerturbGen preserves the **global effective batch** across device counts by dividing the user-specified `--batch_size` by the number of visible GPUs before constructing the DataModule:

```python
# train.py, pre-dataloaders
gpu_number = max(torch.cuda.device_count(), 1)
per_gpu_batch_size = args.batch_size // gpu_number
```

The same arithmetic appears verbatim in `scmaskgit/train.py`, making the invariant stack-wide. Two practical consequences follow. First, `--batch_size 64` on a 4×A100 node yields `per_gpu_batch_size=16` per DDP rank — a documented LPS production run used `--max_len 797 --tgt_vocab_size 2002` at batch 64, and checkpoint filenames embed the *global* batch value (`batch_{args.batch_size}`), not the per-rank value. Second, because floor division is used, device counts that do not divide the batch evenly (e.g., batch 50 across 4 GPUs) silently drop samples per step; keep `--batch_size` a multiple of the target GPU count. The DataModule additionally pins memory, enables persistent workers, and sets `prefetch_factor=4` to keep GPU ranks fed while they stall on gradient all-reduce barriers.

Sources: [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L538-L559), [scmaskgit/train.py](/scmaskgit/train.py#L333-L349), [Dataloaders/datamodule.py](/perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L189-L197)

## Multi-Node and Cluster Launch Path

Multi-node execution is configured through `--num_node` (passed directly as `num_nodes` to the Lightning Trainer) and launched through LSF `BSUB` scripts under `perturbgen/batch_job_script/`. A representative production script for the LPS cohort interpolation run requests **4 exclusive-process NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs**, splits 4 CPU cores per host (`span[ptile=4]`), loads CUDA 12.1.1, and invokes `train.py` with `--num_node 1`. The single-node case requires no additional networking configuration because Lightning's DDP launch handles rank discovery from the scheduler's environment.

```bash
#BSUB -gpu 'mode=exclusive_process:num=4:gmodel=NVIDIAA100_SXM4_80GB'
#BSUB -n 4
#BSUB -R "span[ptile=4]"
module load cuda-12.1.1
python3 .../perturbgen/train.py --train_mode masking ... --batch_size 64 --num_node 1
```

For multi-node jobs, raise both the `-n`/`-gpu` directives per host and `--num_node`; Lightning expects `MASTER_ADDR`/`MASTER_PORT`-capable scheduling, which LSF's GPU queues provide when all ranks land on hosts with the same interconnect. Note that WandB run names gain a UUID suffix whenever `torch.cuda.device_count() > 1` — this prevents checkpoint/log collisions between replicated ranks under [Experiment Tracking with Weights and Biases](20-experiment-tracking-with-weights-and-biases).

| Resource | BSUB Directive | Production Value |
|---|---|---|
| GPUs | `-gpu 'mode=exclusive_process:num=N:gmodel=...'` | 4 × A100 SXM4 80GB |
| CPU cores | `-n` + `-R "span[ptile=4]"` | 4 (one per GPU) |
| CUDA runtime | `module load` | cuda-12.1.1 |
| Memory | `-M` / `-R 'select[mem>...]'` | 50000 MB |
| Nodes | `--num_node` (CLI) | 1 (single-node default) |

Sources: [batch_job_script/lps/interpolation/2_run_train_masking_Encoder_interpolation.sh](/perturbgen/batch_job_script/lps/interpolation/2_run_train_masking_Encoder_interpolation.sh#L3-L16), [batch_job_script/lps/interpolation/2_run_train_masking_Encoder_interpolation.sh](/perturbgen/batch_job_script/lps/interpolation/2_run_train_masking_Encoder_interpolation.sh#L33-L63), [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L628-L630), [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L683-L688)

## Single-GPU and Notebook-Safe Fallback

Distributed launchers spawn processes, which is incompatible with an already-running Jupyter kernel. `train.py` therefore exposes `--single_device`: when set — or when only one CUDA device is visible — the Trainer runs with `devices=1, strategy='auto'`, bypassing DDP/DeepSpeed process groups entirely. The in-process Python API (`pg.train_*`) sets this flag programmatically; multi-GPU training must go through the CLI/batch-script path. Relatedly, `--compile` (default on) torch-compiles the masking model for throughput, but the API disables it because compilation can stall or deadlock inside an interactive kernel — the resulting model is numerically identical either way.

Sources: [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L148-L158), [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L666-L674)

## torch.compile Interop with Checkpoint Resume

Under DDP, Lightning wraps the compiled module, and `torch.compile` renames state-dict keys with a `._orig_mod.` prefix. PerturbGen handles the resulting asymmetry explicitly: `PerturbGenTrainer.on_save_checkpoint` strips the prefix so checkpoints are portable, while `_restore_compiled_keys` re-inserts it on load **only when the live module is compiled** — guaranteeing strict key matching for `trainer.fit(ckpt_path=...)` and `load_from_checkpoint` regardless of whether the resuming process uses the same `--compile` setting as the original run. When porting checkpoints between a DeepSpeed run and a DDP or single-device run, perform the ZeRO→fp32 conversion first; this prefix logic operates purely on the Lightning `state_dict` layer above that.

Sources: [Model/trainer.py](/perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L61-L72), [Model/trainer.py](/perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L123)

## Distributed Data Loading Considerations

`PerturbGenDataModule` deliberately does **not** attach a `DistributedSampler` itself: Lightning injects per-rank sharding automatically for `DataLoader`s returned by `train_dataloader`/`val_dataloader`. The module's own responsibilities are the performance knobs that matter under DDP — `pin_memory=True`, `persistent_workers=True` when `num_workers > 0`, and `prefetch_factor=4`. When `--use_weighted_sampler` is enabled, a `WeightedRandomSampler` with a fixed-seed generator replaces shuffling (and sets `shuffle=False`); under DDP each rank draws from the same weighted distribution while Lightning ensures disjoint sample routing, so class-rebalancing semantics are preserved without manual rank-aware sampling code.

Sources: [Dataloaders/datamodule.py](/perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L189-L197), [Dataloaders/datamodule.py](/perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L295-L313), [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L328-L333)

## Operational Troubleshooting Matrix

| Symptom | Root Cause | Verified Fix in Codebase |
|---|---|---|
| Hang at startup inside Jupyter | Multi-process DDP/DeepSpeed cannot launch in an interactive kernel | Set `--single_device True` or use batch scripts (`train.py` comment, L148-L152) |
| CUDA OOM at ZeRO stage 2 | Optimizer states sharded, parameters replicated | Expected at stage 2; stage-3 not exposed — reduce `--d_model`/`--num_layers` instead |
| Strict-load failure on resume | `._orig_mod.` prefix mismatch after `torch.compile` | Handled by `_restore_compiled_keys` (`Model/trainer.py` L61-L72) |
| Silent per-step sample loss | `batch_size // gpu_number` floor division with non-divisible batch | Keep `--batch_size` divisible by GPU count (`train.py` L538-L540) |
| Checkpoint not loadable outside DeepSpeed | ZeRO shards stored across ranks | Convert with `convert_zero_checkpoint_to_fp32_state_dict` (`scmaskgit/train.py` L32-L34) |
| Duplicate WandB runs across ranks | Rank name collision | Automatic UUID suffix when `device_count() > 1` (`train.py` L628-L630) |

Sources: [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L148-L158), [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L538-L540), [Model/trainer.py](/perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L61-L72), [scmaskgit/train.py](/scmaskgit/train.py#L32-L34), [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L628-L630)

## Recommended Configuration Defaults

For advanced deployments, the repository's own production runs establish a defensible baseline: DDP on 4×A100 80GB with exclusive-process GPU mode, `--batch_size 64` (16/rank), `--n_workers 4` matching `span[ptile=4]` core allocation, CUDA 12.1.1, and `--ckpt_every_n_epochs 5` to bound checkpoint I/O on shared filesystems like Lustre. Prefer DeepSpeed stage 2 when fine-tuning with larger `--d_model` or longer `--max_len` overrides push Adam state memory past the A100 envelope; prefer DDP for the standard 768-dim configuration where its lower latency and simpler checkpoint format win. For validation-side distributed concerns (generation across timepoints, MMD/EMD evaluation), continue to [In Silico Perturbation Modes](10-in-silico-perturbation-modes) and [Evaluation Metrics: MMD, EMD, Optimal Transport](13-evaluation-metrics-mmd-emd-optimal-transport); for the upstream launch scripts and sweep orchestration that invoke these strategies, see [Hyperparameter Sweeps and Batch Jobs](18-hyperparameter-sweeps-and-batch-jobs).

Sources: [batch_job_script/lps/interpolation/2_run_train_masking_Encoder_interpolation.sh](/perturbgen/batch_job_script/lps/interpolation/2_run_train_masking_Encoder_interpolation.sh#L33-L63), [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L334-L339), [train.py](/perturbgen/train.py#L368-L372)

> [!TIP]
> The `find_unused_parameters` flag is intentionally asymmetric between the two stacks (`False` in `perturbgen/train.py`, `True` in `scmaskgit/train.py`). Copying a trainer setup from one stack to the other will either reintroduce unused-parameter scan overhead or crash on frozen encoder branches — always match the flag to the stack.

> [!TIP]
> Checkpoint filenames embed the **global** batch size (`batch_{args.batch_size}`), but training actually consumes `batch_size // gpu_count` per rank. When auditing a pretraining cohort checkpoint from `pretraining_cohort/`, treat the filename's batch value as the global effective batch, not per-device.

# Experiment Tracking with Weights and Biases



PerturbGen uses **Weights & Biases (W&B)** as its single source of truth for training telemetry: every loss curve, perplexity score, and evaluation metric produced during model training flows through W&B's dashboard, and every hyperparameter sweep is orchestrated by a W&B *sweep agent*. This page explains how the tracking layer is wired into the Lightning training entry points, how to configure it via CLI flags and environment variables, how the offline-first default protects cluster jobs, and how to launch and monitor your own hyperparameter sweeps. No prior W&B experience is assumed.

## Tracking Architecture at a Glance

Experiment tracking in PerturbGen follows the standard PyTorch Lightning logger pattern rather than direct `wandb` API calls. The `WandbLogger` class from `pytorch_lightning.loggers` is imported once in the training entry point, configured from three CLI flags (each with an environment-variable fallback), and handed to the `pl.Trainer`. From that moment, every `self.log(..., logger=True)` call inside the two Lightning modules — `PerturbGenTrainer` (masked-token pretraining) and `CountDecoderTrainer` (count prediction) — is transparently forwarded to W&B.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph CLI["train.py CLI layer"]
        ENV["WANDB_MODE / WANDB_ENTITY / WANDB_PROJECT"]
        FLAGS["--wandb_mode / --wandb_entity / --wandb_project"]
        ENV -->|fallback defaults| FLAGS
    end
    FLAGS --> GATE{"mode == 'disabled'?"}
    GATE -->|yes| NOLOG["logger=False<br/>(no W&B process started)"]
    GATE -->|no| WL["WandbLogger<br/>entity, project, name, save_dir, mode"]
    subgraph MODULES["LightningModules"]
        PG["PerturbGenTrainer<br/>perplexity metrics"]
        CD["CountDecoderTrainer<br/>loss / MSE / EMD metrics"]
    end
    PG -->|self.log logger=True| WL
    CD -->|self.log logger=True| WL
    WL -->|mode=online| CLOUD["W&B web dashboard"]
    WL -->|mode=offline| LOCAL["./logs/&lt;run_id&gt;/wandb<br/>(upload later via wandb sync)"]
```

The design deliberately separates *what* is logged (the modules) from *where* it goes (the logger), which means you can switch between online, offline, and fully disabled tracking without touching any model code.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L12-L13), [Model/trainer.py](perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L22-L25)

## Configuring W&B: CLI Flags and Environment Variables

Three flags on `train.py` control the entire W&B setup. Each follows the same precedence rule: the CLI flag wins; if omitted, the corresponding `WANDB_*` environment variable is used; if that is also unset, a hard-coded fallback applies.

| Flag | Environment variable | Default fallback | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--wandb_mode` | `WANDB_MODE` | `offline` | `online`, `offline`, or `disabled` |
| `--wandb_entity` | `WANDB_ENTITY` | *your default W&B entity* | Team or username that owns the project |
| `--wandb_project` | `WANDB_PROJECT` | `perturbgen` | Project name on the W&B dashboard |

The `offline` default is a deliberate operational choice: runs are saved locally and never block on authentication, which matters on shared compute clusters where interactive logins are impractical. In W&B terminology, an **entity** is your user or team namespace, a **project** groups related runs, and a **run** is one execution of a training script.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L168-L194)

## Run Modes: online, offline, disabled

The `--wandb_mode` flag maps directly onto W&B's native modes, plus one special case that is unique to PerturbGen:

| Mode | Behavior | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `online` | Live streaming to the W&B dashboard | Interactive sessions with network access |
| `offline` (default) | Everything written to a local `wandb/` directory; upload later with `wandb sync <run_dir>` | Cluster jobs, shared accounts, unreliable networks |
| `disabled` | **No logger at all** — `trainer` receives `logger=False` instead of a `WandbLogger` | Debugging, tests, notebook runs |

> [!TIP]
> Notice the `disabled` branch does **not** create a `WandbLogger(mode='disabled')` — it passes `logger=False` to the Trainer instead. The code comment explains why: even in `disabled` mode, accessing `WandbLogger.experiment` triggers `wandb.init()`, whose service startup can hang a headless Jupyter kernel. Skipping the logger object entirely sidesteps that failure mode while keeping `self.log` calls and checkpointing functional.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L168-L179), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L620-L626)

## What Gets Logged to Your Runs

Metrics are emitted from the Lightning modules with the `logger=True` flag, which routes them into the active `WandbLogger`. Names use a `stage/metric` convention so the W&B dashboard groups them cleanly. The monitoring key for checkpoint selection is chosen in `train.py` depending on whether a validation split exists:

| Training mode | Logged metrics | Checkpoint monitor |
|---|---|---|
| `masking` (PerturbGenTrainer) | `train/perplexity`, `val/perplexity` (epoch-aggregated variants appear as `..._epoch` in W&B) | `val/perplexity`, else `train/perplexity` |
| `count` (CountDecoderTrainer) | `val/loss`, `val/mse`, `val/emd`, `train/emd` | `val/mse`, else `train/mse` |
| Count-mode testing | `test/loss`, `test/mse` | — |

A few details worth knowing when reading dashboard charts: the EMD values are computed on epoch boundaries over accumulated predictions, subsampled to at most 10,000 cells with a fixed generator seed of 42, so the series is reproducible across runs; and all `self.log` calls for these metrics pass `logger=True`, which is what activates the W&B pipeline.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L583-L619), [Model/trainer.py](perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L1008-L1036), [Model/trainer.py](perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L1047-L1102), [Model/trainer.py](perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L1153-L1179)

## Run Naming and Multi-GPU Safety

Each run gets a timestamp-based identifier of the form `YYYYMMDD_HHMM_cellgen`, and in multi-GPU settings a six-character UUID suffix is appended (`..._a3f2c1`) so that DDP workers launching near-simultaneously do not collide into one run name. Local W&B files land under `save_dir=args.log_dir` (default `logs/`). The same naming pattern appears in the legacy HPO script, which shows the convention predates the current pipeline.

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L574-L576), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L628-L638), [scmaskgit/hpo.py](scmaskgit/hpo.py#L286-L301)

## Hyperparameter Sweeps with a W&B Agent

Sweeps are where W&B becomes more than a passive logger. PerturbGen ships eight ready-made sweep configs under `perturbgen/configs/sweep/` (masking and count variants for the LPS, EB, cytoimmgen, and HSPC datasets). A W&B sweep config declares a **search method** (grid, random, bayes), a **metric to optimize**, the **program** to launch, and a **parameter space** in which fixed values use `value:` and grids use `values:`. The `wandb agent` process then samples configurations from that space and launches one training run per sample.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["1. Edit configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml<br/>grid over cellgen_lr, cellgen_wd, d_ff"] --> B["2. wandb sweep configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml<br/>prints entity/project/SWEEP_ID"]
    B --> C["3. Paste the sweep ID into run_sweep.sh:<br/>wandb agent lotfollahi/ttransformer_sweep/42vqfszc"]
    C --> D["4. BSUB queues the job;<br/>WANDB_DIR exported to $cwd/wandb"]
    D --> E["5. Agent launches one trial =<br/>python train.py with sampled flags"]
    E --> F["6. PerturbGenTrainer logs<br/>val/perplexity each epoch"]
    F --> G{"Grid exhausted?"}
    G -->|no| E
    G -->|yes| H["7. Compare trials in the W&B sweep view<br/>sorted by val/perplexity_epoch, minimize"]
```

Anatomy of the shipped masking sweep config (`sweep-lps-masking.yaml`):

| Key | Example value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `method: grid` | `grid` | Exhaustively evaluates every parameter combination |
| `metric: {goal: minimize, name: val/perplexity_epoch}` | — | The dashboard ranks trials by this exact Lightning key |
| `parameters.*.value` | `train_mode: 'masking'` | Constant across all trials |
| `parameters.*.values` | `cellgen_lr: [1e-5, 5e-4, ...]` | The swept search grid |
| `program:` | absolute path to `train.py` | Script the agent executes per trial |
| `project:` | `ttransformer_sweep` | W&B project that owns the sweep |

> [!TIP]
> Two practical adjustments when reusing these configs: the shipped `program:` and dataset paths are absolute paths from the authors' Lustre filesystem, so replace them with paths valid on your machine (e.g., `perturbgen/train.py` relative to the agent's working directory); and the `metric.name` string must match a logged Lightning key *character-for-character*, or the agent cannot rank trials.

The batch script wraps the agent in an LSF job: it loads CUDA, activates the environment, exports `WANDB_DIR=$cwd/wandb` so run artifacts land on the working filesystem rather than `$HOME`, then starts `wandb agent <entity>/<project>/<sweep_id>`. You only need to substitute your own sweep ID after running step 2.

Sources: [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L1-L26), [sweep-lps-masking.yaml](perturbgen/configs/sweep/sweep-lps-masking.yaml#L1-L75)

## The Legacy Ray Tune + W&B Path

Inside the `scmaskgit` package (the earlier codebase PerturbGen's `PerturbGenTrainer` evolved from), `hpo.py` implements an alternative sweep strategy: **Ray Tune with BOHB** (Bayesian optimization + HyperBand early stopping) instead of a native W&B agent. It demonstrates a different logger configuration worth knowing about: `WandbLogger(project="Moscf", log_model=True, settings=wandb.Settings(save_code=False))` — notably `log_model=True`, which uploads checkpoints as W&B artifacts. Because it was built for a cluster where `$HOME` is not writable, the script pins all five W&B directory environment variables (`WANDB_CACHE_DIR`, `WANDB_CONFIG_DIR`, `WANDB_ARTIFACT_DIR`, `WANDB_DATA_DIR`, `WANDB_ARTIFACT_LOCATION`) to the current working directory. Its search space spans architecture (`d_model`, `num_heads`, `num_layers`, `d_ff`), regularization (`dropout`, `weight_decay`), and optimization (`learning_rate`, `batch_size`) over 20 samples.

For new work, prefer the native `wandb agent` workflow in the previous section — it is the path exercised by the shipped sweep configs — but this file is a useful reference if you need checkpoint artifacts on the dashboard or HyperBand early termination of weak trials.

Sources: [scmaskgit/hpo.py](scmaskgit/hpo.py#L39-L43), [scmaskgit/hpo.py](scmaskgit/hpo.py#L286-L304), [scmaskgit/hpo.py](scmaskgit/hpo.py#L337-L364)

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Training hangs at startup inside Jupyter | `wandb.init()` service startup in a headless kernel | Run with `--wandb_mode disabled` (takes the `logger=False` shortcut) |
| Job blocks waiting for login on the cluster | `--wandb_mode online` without cached credentials | Keep the default `offline`, or run `wandb login` once / set `WANDB_API_KEY` |
| `disk quota exceeded` errors from wandb | W&B cache defaulting to `$HOME` | Export `WANDB_DIR` (and related `WANDB_*_DIR` vars) to a workspace path, as `run_sweep.sh` does |
| Offline runs never appear on the dashboard | Offline mode writes locally by design | Run `wandb sync logs/<run_id>/wandb/<run_name>` after the job finishes |
| Sweep shows no ranked trials | `metric.name` in the YAML does not match a logged key | Use the exact Lightning key, e.g. `val/perplexity_epoch` |
| Duplicate run names in multi-GPU DDP | Several workers initializing simultaneously | Already handled: a UUID suffix is appended when more than one GPU is visible |

Sources: [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L168-L194), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L620-L638), [run_sweep.sh](perturbgen/run_sweep.sh#L20-L24)

## Next Steps

With tracking understood, natural continuations in this catalog are:

- Launch the sweeps you just learned to read on the dashboard: [Hyperparameter Sweeps and Batch Jobs](18-hyperparameter-sweeps-and-batch-jobs)
- Understand where the logged perplexity comes from in the masking objective: [Two-Stage Masking and Count Decoder Training](7-two-stage-masking-and-count-decoder-training)
- Scale tracked runs across nodes while keeping one coherent run: [Distributed Training with DDP and DeepSpeed](19-distributed-training-with-ddp-and-deepspeed)
- Manage the `log_dir` and path variables that ground W&B's local storage: [Configuration System and Path Management](17-configuration-system-and-path-management)

# Python API Reference



This page documents the programmatic Python interface of PerturbGen. The package exposes a deliberately minimal, scvi-tools-style facade in `perturbgen.model`: a module-level `tokenize()` function and a `PerturbGen` model class covering the full lifecycle — tokenization, two-stage training, embedding extraction, in-silico perturbation, and persistence. Everything runs **in-process** (no shell-outs to CLI scripts), so the API is notebook-first by design. This page is a reference: for guided usage see [Quick Start](2-quick-start) and [Tutorial Notebooks Walkthrough](4-tutorial-notebooks-walkthrough), and for the command-line equivalent see [CLI Command Reference](22-cli-command-reference).

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L1-L27), [__init__.py](perturbgen/__init__.py#L1-L6)

## API Layering and Design Model

The public API is a thin, typed facade over the repository's existing entry points. Each `PerturbGen` method synthesizes an argument vector (or, for perturbation, a temporary YAML config) and dispatches to the underlying `main()` function in the same process. This layering gives you a stable, documented surface while the CLI entry points, PyTorch Lightning modules, and data pipeline remain independently usable at a lower level.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph user["Your Notebook / Script"]
        U["import perturbgen as pg"]
    end
    subgraph facade["Public API — perturbgen.model"]
        T["tokenize()"]
        PG["PerturbGen"]
    end
    subgraph entry["Entry points (in-process dispatch)"]
        GF["pp.GF_tokenisation.main(argv)"]
        TR["train.main(argv)"]
        VA["val.main(argv)"]
        PV["Perturb.val.main()  ← --config YAML"]
    end
    subgraph core["Lightning core"]
        LDM["PerturbGenDataModule / PerturbGenDataset"]
        LM["PerturbGenTrainer / CountDecoderTrainer"]
    end
    U --> T
    U --> PG
    T --> GF
    PG -->|"train_masking / train_count"| TR
    PG -->|"get_embeddings"| VA
    PG -->|"perturb"| PV
    TR --> LDM
    VA --> LDM
    PV --> LDM
    LDM --> LM
```

The module docstring states the contract explicitly: the API starts from a tokenized-data directory, everything runs in process, and a CUDA GPU is required for `train_masking()`, `train_count()`, and `perturb()` — the same requirement as the CLI.

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L1-L27), [train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L60-L80)

> [!TIP]
> The entry points call `os.chdir(ROOT)` **at import time** ([train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L27)), which would silently relocate a notebook's working directory. The API neutralizes this with the `_preserve_cwd()` context manager wrapped around every dispatch ([model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L43-L54)). If you bypass the API and import entry points directly, restore `os.getcwd()` yourself — and note that `perturb()` deliberately imports `Perturb/val.py` only *after* making paths absolute, because that module also chdirs at import ([model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L644-L653)).

## Package Exports and Import Surface

The top-level package exports exactly two names via `__all__`, both from `perturbgen.model`. This is the entirety of the supported public interface — deeper modules are considered internal.

| Symbol | Kind | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `perturbgen.PerturbGen` | Class | Trainable/perturbable model handle over one tokenized dataset |
| `perturbgen.tokenize` | Function | Standalone preprocessing: AnnData → tokenized dataset directory |

Usage follows the idiom `import perturbgen as pg`, as documented in the module docstring. The Sphinx API docs ([docs/apidoc/perturbgen](docs/apidoc/perturbgen/perturbgen.rst#L15-L22)) additionally auto-document `perturbgen.model`, `perturbgen.train`, and `perturbgen.val` via `automodule`, but only the two `__all__` exports are the stable contract.

Sources: [__init__.py](perturbgen/__init__.py#L1-L6), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L1-L27), [perturbgen.rst](docs/apidoc/perturbgen/perturbgen.rst#L15-L22)

## Preprocessing: `tokenize()`

`tokenize()` is a **standalone preprocessing step** — no model required. It tokenizes and pairs an AnnData file and returns the tokenized-data directory path, which is what you pass to `PerturbGen()`. It works by synthesizing an argv list and invoking `perturbgen.pp.GF_tokenisation.main()` in-process; output is written under the project's `TOKENIZED_DIR` (see [Configuration System and Path Management](17-configuration-system-and-path-management)).

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L69-L149), [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L30)

**Key parameters:**

| Parameter | Type / Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `adata_path` | `str` | Input AnnData `.h5ad` |
| `dataset` | `str` | Name of the output subdirectory under `TOKENIZED_DIR` |
| `reference_time` | `str` | The source state; source files written as `<reference_time>.dataset` / `.h5ad` |
| `time_obs` | `str` (keyword-only) | `obs` column holding time-point labels |
| `time_point_order` | `Sequence[str]` | Ordered time points; pairs run source → later entries |
| `var_list` | `Sequence[str]` | Metadata variables carried through pairing |
| `main_pairing_obs` | `str` (keyword-only) | Column used for cell pairing |
| `gene_median_path`, `token_dict_path`, `gene_mapping_path` | `str` (keyword-only) | Vocabulary/statistics files; the shipped defaults live in `perturbgen.pp` |
| `n_hvg` | `int = 2000` | Number of highly variable genes |
| `hvg_mode` | `"after_tokenisation"` \| `"before_tokenisation"` | `after_tokenisation` selects exactly `n_hvg` from the Geneformer-tokenizable set; `before_tokenisation` intersects first and yields fewer |
| `pairing_mode` | `"stratified"` \| `"mapping"` | Pairing strategy; `"mapping"` additionally consumes `pairing_file` |
| `overwrite` | `bool = False` | Force re-tokenization; otherwise an existing output is returned as-is |

The function is **idempotent**: if the output already exists it is returned unchanged (a fast no-op on notebook re-runs) unless `overwrite=True`. For the underlying Geneformer-style tokenization mechanics see [Geneformer-Style Gene Tokenization](9-geneformer-style-gene-tokenization) and [Cell Pairing and Data Curation](14-cell-pairing-and-data-curation).

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L69-L149)

## The `PerturbGen` Model Class

`PerturbGen` represents a trained (or trainable) model over exactly one tokenized dataset. Its constructor validates the standard tokenizer layout, auto-detects file-name keys, and records hyperparameters used by all later methods.

### Construction

```python
model = pg.PerturbGen(
    tokenized_dir,               # output of tokenize() or a released dataset
    source="90m_LPS",            # reference time point
    encoder_path="...ckpt",      # optional pretrained encoder
    var_list=["cell_type_harmonized", "cell_pairing_index", "time_after_LPS"],
    pred_tps=[1, 2],
)
```

The constructor infers every file path from the standard layout, using `n_hvg` purely as a filename key (`<n_hvg>_hvg`):

```text
<tokenized_dir>/dataset_<n_hvg>_hvg_src/<source>.dataset
<tokenized_dir>/dataset_<n_hvg>_hvg_tgt/
<tokenized_dir>/h5ad_pairing_<n_hvg>_hvg_src/<source>.h5ad
<tokenized_dir>/h5ad_pairing_<n_hvg>_hvg_tgt/
<tokenized_dir>/token_id_to_genename_<n_hvg>.pkl
<tokenized_dir>/tokenid_to_rowid_<n_hvg>.pkl
```

Paths are stored **absolute** so the entry points' `os.chdir(ROOT)` cannot break them; any missing file raises a `FileNotFoundError` naming the key and expected path.

**Constructor parameters:**

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `tokenized_dir` | required | Tokenized dataset directory |
| `source` | required (keyword-only) | Reference/source time point (e.g. `"90m_LPS"`, `"normal"`) |
| `n_hvg` | `None` | Filename key; `None` auto-detects from `dataset_<n>_hvg_src` folders |
| `encoder_path` | `None` | Pretrained encoder checkpoint (e.g. from the pretraining cohort) |
| `encoder` | `"scmaskgit"` | Encoder architecture selector |
| `n_layers`, `d_ff`, `d_model` | `6`, `64`, `768` | Transformer dimensions |
| `pred_tps` | `(1, 2)` | Predicted time-point indices |
| `var_list` | LPS metadata columns | Metadata variables carried through |
| `context_mode` | `True` | Decoder attends to other time points' observed cells |
| `cond_list` | `None` | Optional conditioning variables |
| `mask_scheduler` | `"pow"` | MaskGIT mask schedule |
| `pos_encoding_mode` | `"time_pos_sin"` | Time-aware positional encoding |
| `loss_mode` | `"zinb"` | Count-decoder loss family |
| `seed` | `42` | Reproducibility seed |
| `max_len`, `tgt_vocab_size` | `None` / `None` | Base sequence length and vocabulary size; leave both `None` to auto-detect, or set **both** to match an explicit-values model (released LPS models: `797` / `2002`) |

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L152-L199), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L200-L239), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L660-L677)

### Training Methods

Training is **two-stage**, mirroring the architecture documented in [Two-Stage Masking and Count Decoder Training](7-two-stage-masking-and-count-decoder-training): `train_masking()` trains the masked generative encoder, then `train_count()` trains the count decoder from a masking checkpoint. Both methods dispatch in-process to `perturbgen.train.main()` and return the metric-best checkpoint path.

| Method | Returns | Checkpoint location | Key knobs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `train_masking(output_dir, ...)` | Best masking `.ckpt` path | `<output_dir>/masking/checkpoints/*.ckpt` (one per epoch) | `max_epochs=20`, `batch_size=64`, `cellgen_lr=1e-4`, `cellgen_wd=1e-4`, `use_weighted_sampler=False`, `ckpt_every_n_epochs=1`, `seed`, `compile=True` |
| `train_count(output_dir, ...)` | Count-decoder `.ckpt` path | `<output_dir>/count/checkpoints/` | `masking_ckpt=None` (defaults to metric-best from step 1), `max_epochs=20`, `count_lr=1e-3`, `count_wd=1e-4`, `mlm_prob=0.15`, `count_dropout=0.0`, `loss_mode` from constructor |

Checkpoint-chaining is automatic: `train_masking()` stores the metric-best checkpoint on the instance, and `train_count()` uses it unless you pass `masking_ckpt=` explicitly (e.g. to pick a specific epoch after inspecting training curves). Calling `train_count()` without any masking checkpoint raises a `ValueError` telling you to run step 1 first. Both methods force `single_device=True` (no DDP) and `wandb_mode="disabled"` in the notebook context — for distributed training and W&B logging use the CLI workflows in [Distributed Training with DDP and DeepSpeed](19-distributed-training-with-ddp-and-deepspeed) and [Experiment Tracking with Weights and Biases](20-experiment-tracking-with-weights-and-biases).

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L284-L324), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L326-L377), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L243-L276)

### Embedding Extraction

`get_embeddings()` extracts gene and/or cell embeddings from a **trained masking model**, writing embedding AnnData files under `output_dir` and returning that path. It dispatches to `perturbgen.val.main()` with `--test_mode masking`.

| Parameter | Default | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `masking_ckpt` | `None` | Falls back to the instance's checkpoint from `train_masking()`; absent both → `ValueError` |
| `return_cell_embs` | `True` | Cell embeddings |
| `return_gene_embs` | `True` | **Requires** `gene_embs_condition` |
| `gene_embs_condition` | `None` | `obs` column; gene embeddings are extracted per unique value (e.g. `"time_after_LPS"`) |
| `batch_size`, `n_workers` | `64`, `4` | Throughput controls |

The coupling between `return_gene_embs` and `gene_embs_condition` is validated eagerly: requesting gene embeddings without a condition column raises a `ValueError` with the suggested remedy. For interpretation of the outputs see [Cell and Gene Embedding Extraction](11-cell-and-gene-embedding-extraction) and downstream analyses in [Gene Program Discovery](12-gene-program-discovery).

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L382-L458)

### In Silico Perturbation: `perturb()`

`perturb()` runs in-silico perturbation of named genes through the count decoder and writes predicted h5ads to `output_dir`. It builds a full YAML config dict in memory, writes it to a temporary file, and drives `perturbgen.Perturb.val.main()` in-process by swapping `sys.argv` (restored in a `finally` block).

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `genes` | required | Ensembl IDs to perturb, e.g. `["ENSG00000125538"]` (IL1B) |
| `mode` | `"knockout"` | See mode table below |
| `where` | `"source"` | `"source"` edits the source state and propagates downstream; `"target"` edits a target state |
| `pert_tps` | `None` | With `where="target"`: which predicted time points' target states to perturb (e.g. `[1]`); **required** for target `knockout`/`delete`/`pad` |
| `pred_tps` | constructor's | Predicted time points |
| `n_samples` | `3` | Count draws from the count decoder per cell, averaged into predicted counts (`1` = predicted mean) |
| `count_ckpt` | `None` | Falls back to instance checkpoint; absent both → `ValueError` |
| `context_mode` | `False` | Perturbation prediction default; `True` lets the decoder attend to observed unperturbed cells of other time points |
| `extra_config` | `None` | Escape hatch into raw config keys (below) |
| `temperature`, `iterations` | `1.5`, `19` | **Inert** — accepted for backward compatibility only |

**Perturbation modes** (API alias → underlying `perturbation_mode`):

| API `mode` | Internal value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `"knockout"` | `"mask"` | Default; aliased from mask |
| `"mask"` | `"mask"` | Direct alias |
| `"overexpress"` | `"overexpress"` | The only target-mode edit that does not require `pert_tps` |
| `"delete"` | `"delete"` | Target usage requires `pert_tps` |
| `"pad"` | `"pad"` | Target usage requires `pert_tps` |

`where` maps to `perturbation_sequence` via `source→src`, `target→tgt`. Mode semantics are covered conceptually in [In Silico Perturbation Modes](10-in-silico-perturbation-modes).

**`extra_config`** injects options of the raw perturbation config (`perturbgen/Perturb/val.py`) that `perturb()` does not manage, as `{section: {key: value}}` with sections `"data"`, `"trainer"`, `"datamodule"`, or `"model"`. The API enforces ownership: keys that `perturb()` already sets are **rejected** with a `ValueError` listing the clash (only `num_workers` in `datamodule` is considered a safe override). Notable extras documented in the docstring: `data.filter_var`/`data.filter_cond` (e.g. `{"filter_var": "drug", "filter_cond": ["Drug10"]}`), and `data.perturb_genes_file` together with `perturb_colname`/`perturb_cluster` for cluster-wise gene perturbation (pass `genes=[]` alongside).

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L486-L542), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L57-L66), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L543-L657)

> [!TIP]
> `temperature` and `iterations` configure MaskGIT generation (`validation_mode="generate"`), but `perturb()` **always runs** `validation_mode="inference"`, which decodes the observed target cells — matching the released LPS and HSPC perturbation configs. If you pass non-default values the API emits a `UserWarning` rather than silently ignoring them ([model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L558-L563)). To actually sample with MaskGIT dynamics, use the generate mode of the CLI instead ([CLI Command Reference](22-cli-command-reference)).

Also note the docstring's practical constraint: for a **source knockout** the target gene must be expressed in the source state, otherwise every cell is filtered out.

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L539-L542)

### Persistence: `save()` / `load()`

Persistence is manifest-based, not weight-based: `save(path)` writes a `perturbgen_model.json` containing the tokenized-dir, source, `n_hvg`, hyperparameters, and checkpoint locations; `PerturbGen.load(path)` reconstructs the instance from it. The heavy model weights stay in the referenced `.ckpt` files, so a manifest is small and portable, and `load()` re-validates the tokenized layout through the constructor. `train_masking`/`train_count`/`perturb` also expose graceful fallbacks via `_latest_ckpt()`, which picks the most recently modified `.ckpt` if the metric-best is missing.

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L463-L481), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L680-L688)

## End-to-End Object Lifecycle

The full lifecycle, as documented in the module docstring, is a five-call pipeline. Each stage's return value feeds the next, and the manifest lets you stop/resume at any boundary:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["AnnData .h5ad"] -->|"pg.tokenize()"| B["tokenized dir"]
    B -->|"PerturbGen(...)"| C["model handle"]
    C -->|"train_masking()"| D["masking ckpt"]
    D -->|"train_count()"| E["count ckpt"]
    C -->|"get_embeddings()"| F["embedding AnnData"]
    E -->|"perturb()"| G["perturbed h5ads"]
    C <-.->|"save() / load()"| H["perturbgen_model.json"]
```

```python
import perturbgen as pg

model = pg.PerturbGen(
    "T_perturb/tokenized_data/lps_90min_perturb",
    source="90m_LPS",
    encoder_path="pretraining_cohort/....ckpt",
    var_list=["cell_type_harmonized", "cell_pairing_index", "time_after_LPS"],
    pred_tps=[1, 2],
)
masking_ckpt = model.train_masking(output_dir="lps_model", max_epochs=20, batch_size=64)
count_ckpt = model.train_count(output_dir="lps_model", masking_ckpt=masking_ckpt)
model.save("lps_model")                       # or: pg.PerturbGen.load("lps_model")

pred = model.perturb(genes=["ENSG00000125538"],   # IL1B
                     mode="knockout", where="source")
```

The config-building logic of `perturb()` is exercised directly by the test suite, which constructs a fake tokenized directory, mocks `Perturb.val.main`, and asserts on the generated YAML — a useful executable specification of the API's contract ([test_api_perturb.py](perturbgen/tests/test_api_perturb.py#L1-L60)); see [Test and Benchmark Suite](26-test-and-benchmark-suite).

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L4-L20), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L8-L20), [test_api_perturb.py](perturbgen/tests/test_api_perturb.py#L28-L40)

## Lower-Level Module Surface

For advanced use — custom training loops, research extensions, or debugging — the layers beneath the facade are directly importable. These are internal and evolve faster than the public API.

| Module | Key symbols | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `perturbgen.Model.trainer` | `PerturbGenTrainer`, `CountDecoderTrainer` | `LightningModule`s with ~50 hyperparameters: vocab size, heads/layers, mask schedule, precision, checkpoint-key handling for `torch.compile` ([Model/trainer.py](perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L75-L124)) |
| `perturbgen.Dataloaders.datamodule` | `PerturbGenDataset`, `PerturbGenDataModule` | `torch Dataset` + `LightningDataModule` over HF `datasets`; src/tgt time-step pairing, count tensors, condition encodings, optional `WeightedRandomSampler` ([datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L151-L226)) |
| `perturbgen.Modules.transformer` | `PerturbGen`, `CountDecoder` | Transformer encoder/decoder implementations |
| `perturbgen.train` | `main(argv)` | argparse entry point; `--train_mode {masking, count}`, splitting, DDP/DeepSpeed strategies ([train.py](perturbgen/train.py#L60-L74)) |
| `perturbgen.val` / `perturbgen.Perturb.val` | `main(argv)` / `main()` | Validation/embedding entry; perturbation entry reading `--config <yaml>` |
| `perturbgen.pp` | `GF_tokenisation`, `tokenizer`, vocabulary `.pkl` constants | Geneformer-style tokenization; `pp` package constants point at the shipped `gene_median`, `token_dict`, and `ensembl_mapping` files ([pp/__init__.py](perturbgen/pp/__init__.py#L1-L7)); the raw `TranscriptomeTokenizer` docstring documents input formats and the 95M-series settings (`special_token=True`, `model_input_size=4096`) ([tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L1-L39)) |
| `perturbgen.src` | `losses`, `metric`, `mmd`, `optimal_transport`, `utils`, `gf_utils` | Loss functions, distributional metrics ([Evaluation Metrics](13-evaluation-metrics-mmd-emd-optimal-transport)), embedding/attn utilities |
| `perturbgen.configs.paths` | `ROOT`, `REPO_DIR`, `TOKENIZED_DIR`, `ENCODER_CKPT_PATH`, `GENE_MEDIAN_PATH`, ... | Path defaults; `TOKENIZED_DIR` is where `tokenize()` writes, and `ENCODER_CKPT_PATH` points at the shipped pretraining checkpoint ([paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L3-L16)) |

Sources: [Model/trainer.py](perturbgen/Model/trainer.py#L75-L124), [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L22-L36), [pp/__init__.py](perturbgen/pp/__init__.py#L1-L7), [tokenizer.py](perturbgen/pp/tokenizer.py#L1-L39), [paths.py](perturbgen/configs/paths.py#L3-L35)

## Error Contracts and Invariants

The API fails loudly and early, with actionable messages rather than silent misconfiguration:

| Raised at | Condition | Exception |
|---|---|---|
| `PerturbGen(...)` | `max_len` set without `tgt_vocab_size` (or vice versa) | `ValueError` |
| `PerturbGen(...)` | Any expected tokenized file missing for the given `source`/`n_hvg` | `FileNotFoundError` (names the path) |
| `n_hvg` auto-detection | No `dataset_<n>_hvg_src` folder, or multiple `n_hvg` variants side by side | `FileNotFoundError` / `ValueError` |
| `train_count()` | No masking checkpoint available or passed | `ValueError` |
| `get_embeddings()` | `return_gene_embs=True` without `gene_embs_condition` | `ValueError` |
| `perturb()` | No count checkpoint; invalid `mode`/`where`; `where="target"` with non-overexpress mode but no `pert_tps` | `ValueError` |
| `perturb()` `extra_config` | Unknown section, non-dict values, or keys owned by `perturb()` | `ValueError` / `TypeError` |
| `PerturbGenDataModule` | `use_weighted_sampler=True` without `sampling_keys` | `ValueError` |

**Invariants** worth remembering: `tokenize()` is idempotent by default; all stored paths are absolute and immune to the entry points' `os.chdir(ROOT)`; method chaining is automatic (metric-best masking checkpoint flows into `train_count()`); and the returned path strings from every method are the canonical handles you pass onward — nothing needs to be re-derived by hand.

Sources: [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L200-L239), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L352-L357), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L399-L411), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L543-L575), [model.py](perturbgen/model.py#L628-L639), [datamodule.py](perturbgen/Dataloaders/datamodule.py#L219-L224)
